\label{def:tk-theory-package}
Assume \textbf{A\_FIN}. A \emph{finite theory package} is a tuple
\[
\mathcal T \;=\; (Z,\ f,\ \Sigma_f,\ E,\ \mathcal A)
\]
where:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $Z$ is a finite carrier set (microstate space).
  \item $f:Z\to X$ is a \emph{lens} (coarse description). The induced definability structure $\Sigma_f$ is the finite $\sigma$-algebra (equivalently, partition) on $Z$ generated by $f$, i.e.\ the family of predicates measurable with respect to $f$.
  \item $E:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$ is a \emph{completion/packaging endomap} on a chosen space of descriptions $\mathcal V$ associated to $Z$.
  Typically $E$ is idempotent ($E\circ E=E$) or approximately idempotent in a specified norm.
  In the empirical/dynamical instantiation $\mathcal V=\Delta(Z)$, while in the order-theoretic instantiation $\mathcal V=Z$ (with $E$ a closure operator).
  \item $\mathcal A$ is an \emph{audit functional} (a certificate of directionality or drive) defined on the relevant objects in context (e.g.\ path laws for a Markov dynamics, or antisymmetric edge 1-forms on a support graph), together with a designated monotonicity principle under coarse observation: for any further coarsening $g:X\to Y$, the induced pushforward should not increase the audit, schematically
  \[
  \mathcal A\big((g\circ f)_\#(\cdot)\big)\ \le\ \mathcal A\big(f_\#(\cdot)\big),
  \]
  whenever both sides are defined.
\end{itemize}
We call $\Sigma_f$ the \emph{expressive content} of the theory and $E$ its \emph{completion rule}; the fixed points of $E$ are the internally complete descriptions/objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale and lens.

A \emph{closure ladder} is a sequence of closure operators $(c_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ on $L$ such that
$c_n \prec c_{n+1}$ for all $n$. The fixed-point sets form a nested chain

by Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-antitone}.

\label{def:D-IC-01}
Let $Q_f:\Delta(Z)\to \Delta(X)$ be the pushforward (coarse-graining) map
\[
(Q_f\mu)(x) \;:=\; \sum_{z\in B_x}\mu(z).
\]
Fix a \emph{canonical lift} $U_f:\Delta(X)\to \Delta(Z)$ specified by a choice of
\emph{prototype} distributions $(u_x)_{x\in X}$ with $\mathrm{supp}(u_x)\subseteq B_x$ and
$\sum_{z\in B_x}u_x(z)=1$, by setting
\[
(U_f\nu)(z) \;:=\; \sum_{x\in X}\nu(x)\,u_x(z).
\]
Equivalently, $U_f\delta_x=u_x$ and $Q_f U_f = \mathrm{id}_{\Delta(X)}$.

\paragraph{Existence Requires Choosing a Scale.}
For an integer time scale $\tau\ge 1$, define the \emph{induced empirical endomap}
\[
E_{\tau,f}:\Delta(Z)\to \Delta(Z),
\qquad
E_{\tau,f}(\mu) \;:=\; U_f\bigl(Q_f(\mu P^\tau)\bigr).
\]

The (forward) length- T path law P_ rho,T is the probability measure on Z^ T+1 defined by P_ rho,T (z_0, ,z_T) := rho(z_0) _ t=0 ^ T-1 P(z_t,z_ t+1 ). Let R:Z^ T+1 → Z^ T+1 be the reversal map R(z_0, ,z_T)=(z_T, ,z_0) , and write R_ * mu for pushforward of a measure mu . Define the (finite-horizon) path reversal asymmetry Sigma_T(rho) := D_ KL ( P_ rho,T \| R_ * P_ rho,T )∈[0,∈fty]. We use the standard convention D_ KL (p\|q)=+∈fty if p is not absolutely continuous with respect to q .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Fix a horizon $T\in \mathbb N$ with $T\ge 1$ and an initial distribution $\rho\in\Delta(Z)$.
The (forward) length-$T$ path law $\mathbb P_{\rho,T}$ is the probability measure on $Z^{T+1}$ defined by
\[
\mathbb P_{\rho,T}(z_0,\dots,z_T)
:= \rho(z_0)\prod_{t=0}^{T-1} P(z_t,z_{t+1}).
\]
Let $\mathcal R:Z^{T+1}\to Z^{T+1}$ be the reversal map $\mathcal R(z_0,\dots,z_T)=(z_T,\dots,z_0)$, and write $\mathcal{R}_{*}\mu$ for pushforward of a measure $\mu$.
Define the (finite-horizon) \emph{path reversal asymmetry}
\[
\Sigma_T(\rho)\;:=\; D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(\mathbb P_{\rho,T}\,\middle\|\,\mathcal{R}_{*}\mathbb P_{\rho,T}\right)\in[0,\infty].
\]
We use the standard convention $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=+\infty$ if $p$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to $q$.

\textbf{D-PROT-02.}\par
Fix $\alpha\in[0,1]$ and define an autonomous Markov chain on the product space $Z:=X\times \Phi$ by

:=\alpha\,\mathbf{1}_{x'=x}\,\mathsf{S}\,(\phi,\phi')

conclusion: A (Boolean) predicate is a function h:Z→\ 0,1\ . We say that h is definable from the theory f (equivalently: Pi_f -measurable) if it is constant on each block: x∈ X,\ z,z'∈ B_x, h(z)=h(z'). Equivalently, there exists h:X→\ 0,1\ with h= h f .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A (Boolean) \emph{predicate} is a function $h:Z\to\{0,1\}$.
We say that $h$ is \emph{definable from the theory $f$} (equivalently: $\Pi_f$-measurable) if it is constant on each block:
\[
\forall x\in X,\ \forall z,z'\in B_x,\quad h(z)=h(z').
\]
Equivalently, there exists $\tilde h:X\to\{0,1\}$ with $h=\tilde h\circ f$.

conclusion: [P1: operator rewrite] P1 is a rewrite of the substrate operator: replace a Markov kernel P by a new kernel P' (or a finite family \ P^ (m) \ ), thereby changing the endomap mu↦ mu P^tau and the induced empirical endomap E_ tau,f . This is a change in the operator itself, not an external schedule. [P2: gating / constraints] P2 restricts the support graph by deleting edges (setting selected P_ ij =0 ) and renormalizing rows, or equivalently restricting to a subgraph on which the kernel lives. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{definition}[P1: operator rewrite]
P1 is a rewrite of the substrate operator: replace a Markov kernel $P$ by a new kernel $P'$ (or a
finite family $\{P^{(m)}\}$), thereby changing the endomap $\mu\mapsto \mu P^\tau$ and the induced
empirical endomap $E_{\tau,f}$. This is a change in the operator itself, not an external schedule.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[P2: gating / constraints]
P2 restricts the support graph by deleting edges (setting selected $P_{ij}=0$) and renormalizing
rows, or equivalently restricting to a subgraph on which the kernel lives. Cycle-rank claims are
interpreted on the undirected support graph justified by \textbf{A\_REV}.
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:tk-bridge-ports}
A \emph{port space} is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space $U$ with inner product
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_U$ and norm $\|\cdot\|_U$.
Fix a finite time horizon $T>0$ and write $\mathcal U := L^2([0,T];U)$ for square-integrable $U$-valued signals.
A (deterministic) \emph{bridge operator} is a map $\mathsf Z:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U$.
It is \emph{causal} if for all $t\in[0,T]$ and all $u,v\in\mathcal U$,
\[
u(\tau)=v(\tau)\ \text{for a.e.\ }\tau\in[0,t]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (\mathsf Z u)(\tau)=(\mathsf Z v)(\tau)\ \text{for a.e.\ }\tau\in[0,t].
\]
Given an input $u\in\mathcal U$ and output $y=\mathsf Z u$, define the instantaneous supply rate
\[
p(t):=\langle u(t),y(t)\rangle_U,\qquad p^+(t):=\max\{p(t),0\},
\]
and the positive supplied work over $[s,t]\subseteq[0,T]$ by
\[
W^+[s,t]:=\int_s^t p^+(\tau)\,d\tau.
\]

\label{def:tk-passive-storage}
A causal bridge $\mathsf Z:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U$ is \emph{passive with storage} (cf.\ \cite{Willems1972}) if there exist:
(i) a state space $X$, (ii) a nonnegative storage functional $S:X\to[0,\infty)$,
and (iii) for each input $u\in\mathcal U$ a state trajectory $x_u:[0,T]\to X$,
such that for all $0\le s\le t\le T$,
\[
S(x_u(t)) - S(x_u(s))\ \le\ \int_s^t \langle u(\tau),(\mathsf Z u)(\tau)\rangle_U\,d\tau.
\tag{D-TK-BRG-02}\label{eq:tk-passivity}
\]

\label{def:ect-atom}
Fix a port space $U$ and a finite horizon $T>0$, and write $\mathcal U:=L^2([0,T];U)$.
Let $\mathsf Z:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U$ be a causal bridge (Definition~\ref{def:tk-bridge-ports}).
An \emph{atomic (sector) decomposition} of $\mathsf Z$ is a representation
\[
\mathsf Z \;=\; \sum_{r=1}^m \mathsf Z_r
\]
as a parallel sum of causal bridges $\mathsf Z_r:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U$ on the same port space (so $(\mathsf Zu)(t)=\sum_r(\mathsf Z_ru)(t)$).
We call $m$ the \emph{mode count} of the chosen decomposition.
In depth-indexed settings we write $\mathsf Z=\mathsf Z_j$ and denote the mode count by $m_j$.

\label{def:ect-gate}
Fix a finite horizon $T>0$, a port Hilbert space $U_j$, and write $\mathcal U_j:=L^2([0,T];U_j)$.
Let $G_j:U_j\to U_j$ be a self-adjoint positive semidefinite operator.
Define the feasible input class
\[
\mathcal U_j^{\mathrm{feas}}:=\{u\in\mathcal U_j:\ u(t)\in \mathrm{Ran}(G_j)\ \text{for a.e.\ }t\},
\]
the pointwise seminorm on $U_j$,
\[
|v|_{X_j}^2\ :=\ \langle v,G_j v\rangle\quad (v\in U_j),
\]
and the associated integrated energy on a window $[s,t]$,
\[
|u|_{L^2_X(s,t)}^2\ :=\ \int_s^t |u(\tau)|_{X_j}^2\,d\tau.
\]
On $\mathcal U_j^{\mathrm{feas}}$ this is a genuine norm, since the feasibility constraint removes the kernel of $G_j$.

\label{def:ect-sectorization}
Fix a depth $j$ and a port Hilbert space $U_j$.
A \emph{sectorization} is the choice of a finite index set $Q_j$ and a family of orthogonal projections
$\{\Pi_{j,q}:U_j\to U_j\}_{q\in Q_j}$ such that $\Pi_{j,q}\Pi_{j,q'}=0$ for $q\ne q'$ and $\sum_{q\in Q_j}\Pi_{j,q}=I$.
We extend $\Pi_{j,q}$ pointwise to signals $u\in\mathcal U_j:=L^2([0,T];U_j)$ by $(\Pi_{j,q}u)(t):=\Pi_{j,q}(u(t))$.
A causal bridge $\mathsf Z_j:\mathcal U_j\to \mathcal U_j$ is \emph{sector-respecting} if
\[
\mathsf Z_j \;=\; \sum_{q\in Q_j} \Pi_{j,q}\,\mathsf Z_j\,\Pi_{j,q},
\]
i.e.\ the output on each sector depends only on the input restricted to that sector (no cross-sector coupling).

\label{def:level-trichotomy}
For each role \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}, we distinguish
\begin{itemize}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item the \emph{behavioral level}: status, occurrence, or observed
    behavior of the role in a description;
  \item the \emph{verification level}: proof, witness, certificate, or
    checkable record supporting a behavioral
    claim~\citep{MartinLof1984};
  \item the \emph{structural-categorical level}: reusable structure
    supporting the primitive role.
\end{itemize}
Forgetting proceeds from structural-categorical to verification to
behavioral and is lossy. Lifting proceeds from behavioral to
verification to structural-categorical only after adding explicitly
recorded data, and selected lifts are not unique.

\label{def:decomposition-record}
A \emph{decomposition/exhaustion record} for \(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) is a tuple
\[
\Dec{D} = \bigl(\Raw{D},\; (\Chan{i}{D}, \Status{i}{D})_{i=1}^{6},\;
\Residual{D},\; \mathrm{Classify},\; \mathcal{L},\; \mathcal{V},\;
\Audit{D},\; \mathcal{N}\bigr)
\]
where
\begin{itemize}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item the six role channels together with their statuses form the
    six-channel status sequence. If \(\Status{i}{D} = \texttt{active\_projection}\), the channel
    carries an active projection \(\pi_i(D)\) with its full attachment
    data. If \(\Status{i}{D}\) is inactive, the channel carries the
    corresponding below-threshold, collapsed-boundary,
    absent-with-record, or outside-scope status record;
  \item \(\Residual{D} \subseteq \Raw{D}\) is the residual feature set
    (the raw records and annotations not already accounted for by an
    active projection or an inactive status record), and
    \(\mathrm{Classify}\) assigns to each \(r \in \Residual{D}\) a label
    in the scheme of Definition~\ref{def:residual-scheme};
  \item \(\mathcal{L}\) collects the loss and lift records for any level
    crossings involved in projections or classifications;
  \item \(\mathcal{V}\) collects instrument-visibility and
    empirical-bridge annotations where these are asserted;
  \item \(\Audit{D}\) is the honest bookkeeping subrecord;
  \item \(\mathcal{N}\) is the explicit nonclaim record.
\end{itemize}
A decomposition/exhaustion record is \emph{well-formed} when each
\(\Status{i}{D}\) is drawn from the five values of
Definition~\ref{def:channel-status}, each active
\(\pi_i(D)\) is admissible in the sense of
Definitions~\ref{def:role-projection} and~\ref{def:threshold-attachment},
each inactive status record is honestly supported by the corresponding
raw-feature situation, and every raw feature is accounted for at the
channel/exhaustion level either by an active projection, by a status
record for its channel, or by a residual classification. The records in
\(\mathcal{L}\) and \(\mathcal{V}\) are auxiliary annotations on this
coverage, not additional role channels.

conclusion: A hiddenness interface I consists of a closure carrier H_I , a current quotient _I: H_I→ Q_I , a predictive quotient _I: H_I→ M_I refining _I , and the following predicates: determiningStateTyped(I), minimalRelevantUpstream(I), lawfulCurrentExposure(I), together with QuotientExposed(I), PredictiveCollapse(I), PredictiveSurplus(I), HiddenFromCurrent(I). The hidden-from-current predicate records that one current fiber contains at least two predictive classes. The quotient-exposed predicate records that the lawful exposure quotient removes exactly those predictive splits. The hiddenness normal form is the five-conjunct property HiddennessNormalForm(I) := determiningStateTyped(I) minimalRelevantUpstream(I) (lawfulCurrentExposure(I) QuotientExposed(I) ) (PredictiveCollapse(I) lawfulCurrentExposure(I) ) (PredictiveSurplus(I) HiddenFromCurrent(I) ).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:hiddenness-exposure}
A \emph{hiddenness interface} \(I\) consists of a closure carrier
\(\mathcal H_I\), a current quotient
\(\currQ_I:\mathcal H_I\to Q_I\), a predictive quotient
\(\predM_I:\mathcal H_I\to M_I\) refining \(\currQ_I\), and the
following predicates:
\[
  \operatorname{determiningStateTyped}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{minimalRelevantUpstream}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I),
\]
together with
\[
  \operatorname{QuotientExposed}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{PredictiveCollapse}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(I).
\]
The hidden-from-current predicate records that one current fiber
contains at least two predictive classes.  The quotient-exposed
predicate records that the lawful exposure quotient removes exactly
those predictive splits.  The hiddenness normal form is the
five-conjunct property
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{HiddennessNormalForm}(I)
  :={}&
  \operatorname{determiningStateTyped}(I)
  \wedge
  \operatorname{minimalRelevantUpstream}(I)\\
  &{}\wedge
  \bigl(\operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I)
    \leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{QuotientExposed}(I)\bigr)\\
  &{}\wedge
  \bigl(\operatorname{PredictiveCollapse}(I)
    \leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I)\bigr)\\
  &{}\wedge
  \bigl(\operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(I)
    \leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(I)\bigr).
\end{align*}

source_wording_tex:
An endogenous closure system, or E-system, is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:esystem}
 \mathbb S=(\mathcal T,I_S,\Lambda_S,\mathfrak R_S),
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal T\) is a formed package, \(I_S\) a carried instrument,
\(\Lambda_S\) a carried ledger of budgets, prices, and statused residuals,
and \(\mathfrak R_S\) a carried generator mapping certified defect records
to candidate typed P1--P5 repair moves.  A lawful occurrence separately
requires instrument permission, ledger membership, move admissibility, and
realization in the carrier kernel.

conclusion: Let w=(v_0,v_1, ,v_k) be a finite walk with v_k=v_0 and \ v_i,v_ i+1 \ ∈ E for all i . The closed-walk sum of a along w is S_a(w) = _ i=0 ^ k-1 a(v_i,v_ i+1 ). When a is a log-ratio 1 -form, S_a(w) is the (log) cycle affinity. This is the standard cycle-affinity language for finite Markov networks .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Let $w=(v_0,v_1,\dots,v_k)$ be a finite walk with $v_k=v_0$ and
$\{v_i,v_{i+1}\}\in E$ for all $i$.
The \emph{closed-walk sum} of $a$ along $w$ is
\[
S_a(w)\;=\;\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} a(v_i,v_{i+1}).
\]
When $a$ is a log-ratio $1$-form, $S_a(w)$ is the (log) cycle affinity.
This is the standard cycle-affinity language for finite Markov networks \citep{Schnakenberg1976}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (closure package).}
A \emph{closure package} is a pair
\[
\mathrm{pkg}=(X,\operatorname{op})
\]
where $\operatorname{op}\colon X\to X$ is idempotent:
\[
\operatorname{op}(\operatorname{op}(x))=\operatorname{op}(x)\qquad \text{for all }x\in X.

\paragraph{Definition (package change).}
Given two closure packages
\[
\mathrm{pkg}=(X,\operatorname{op}), \qquad \mathrm{pkg}'=(X,\operatorname{op}'),
\]
a \emph{package change} from $\mathrm{pkg}$ to $\mathrm{pkg}'$ is any replacement for which
\[
\operatorname{op}\neq \operatorname{op}'
\]
as endomaps on $X$. A \emph{package-change witness} is a point $x\in X$ such that
\[
\operatorname{op}(x)\neq \operatorname{op}'(x).
\]
The present paper does not formalize the full internal mechanics of such changes. Instead it records the structural fact that genuine strict growth cannot be attributed to a fixed package once idempotent saturation has been proved. Package change is therefore the theorem-track locus at which \(P1/P2\) enter.

and

The functions \(Y_s\) and \(K_s\) are the yield and cost functionals of the slice, and \(C_s\) is its support cone.

\operatorname{AgreeOnCone}_{C_s}(e,c).

\label{def:presentation}
A \emph{finite pointed membership presentation} is a triple $P=(V,\to,v)$ where $V$ is a
finite set of nodes, ${\to}\subseteq V\times V$ is acyclic, and $v\in V$ is a distinguished
\emph{point}. We read $u\to w$ as ``$w$ is a member-candidate of $u$,'' and write
$\Ch_P(u):=\{w: u\to w\}$. The carrier $Z$ is the set of all finite pointed membership
presentations.

\label{def:fg}
An operator $G$ on families of sets is a \emph{completion rule} if $A\subseteq G(A)$ always.

A completion rule that adds only finite sets whose members are drawn from the current family and the transitive closures of its members; see Definition . The one-sorted membership structure obtained from the staged two-sorted presentation by forgetting the explicit stage sort; see Definition . The four named infinitary commitments C-INF, C-POW, C-REPL, and C-SEL; see S . They are hypotheses, not conclusions. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{description}[style=multiline,leftmargin=!,labelwidth=0.31\textwidth,labelsep=0.8em,itemsep=3pt]
\item[Theory package.] A carrier, lens, packaging endomap, and audit
$(Z,f,E,\mathcal A)$; see Convention~\ref{conv:package}. In this paper the package is used only
as an organizing instrument for set-theoretic constructions.
\item[Finite membership presentation.] A finite pointed acyclic graph
$(V,\to,v)$ read as a membership presentation; see Definition~\ref{def:presentation}.
\item[Membership-profile lens.] The map $f\colon Z\to\mathrm{HF}$ sending a presentation to the
decoration of its point; see Definition~\ref{def:lens}. Its definability content is what the
instrument can see.
\item[Packaging map.] The endomap $E(P)=C(f(P))$ that forgets accidental presentation shape and
reinstantiates the profile canonically; see Definition~\ref{def:E}.
\item[Rank audit.] The certificate $\rho(P)=\operatorname{rank}(f(P))$, decreasing along membership edges; see
Definition~\ref{def:rank} and Lemma~\ref{lem:L3}.
\item[Finite packaging operator.] The operator $F$ on subfamilies of $\mathrm{HF}$ generated by empty
set, pairing, flattening, finite gates, and finite transport; see Definition~\ref{def:F}.
\item[Finitely generated completion rule.] A completion rule that adds only finite sets whose
members are drawn from the current family and the transitive closures of its members; see
Definition~\ref{def:fg}.
\item[Rank-erased shadow.] The one-sorted membership structure obtained from the staged
two-sorted presentation by forgetting the explicit stage sort; see Definition~\ref{def:staged}.
\item[Assumption box.] The four named infinitary commitments
\textbf{C-INF}, \textbf{C-POW}, \textbf{C-REPL}, and \textbf{C-SEL}; see
\S\ref{ssec:box}. They are hypotheses, not conclusions.
\item[Strict theory extension.] A package change whose new object map does not factor through the
old ground object; in this paper it is instantiated by Theorem~\ref{thm:nonfactor}.
\item[Ground lens.] The countable ground model read through its coded reals
$\Sig_M=2^\omega\cap M$; see Definition~\ref{def:groundlens}.
\end{description}

\begin{description}[style=multiline,leftmargin=!,labelwidth=0.31\textwidth,labelsep=0.8em,itemsep=3pt]
\item[Theory package.] A carrier, lens, packaging endomap, and audit
$(Z,f,E,\mathcal A)$; see Convention~\ref{conv:package}. In this paper the package is used only
as an organizing instrument for set-theoretic constructions.
\item[Finite membership presentation.] A finite pointed acyclic graph
$(V,\to,v)$ read as a membership presentation; see Definition~\ref{def:presentation}.
\item[Membership-profile lens.] The map $f\colon Z\to\HF$ sending a presentation to the
decoration of its point; see Definition~\ref{def:lens}. Its definability content is what the
instrument can see.
\item[Packaging map.] The endomap $E(P)=C(f(P))$ that forgets accidental presentation shape and
reinstantiates the profile canonically; see Definition~\ref{def:E}.
\item[Rank audit.] The certificate $\rho(P)=\rank(f(P))$, decreasing along membership edges; see
Definition~\ref{def:rank} and Lemma~\ref{lem:L3}.
\item[Finite packaging operator.] The operator $F$ on subfamilies of $\HF$ generated by empty
set, pairing, flattening, finite gates, and finite transport; see Definition~\ref{def:F}.
\item[Finitely generated completion rule.] A completion rule that adds only finite sets whose
members are drawn from the current family and the transitive closures of its members; see
Definition~\ref{def:fg}.
\item[Rank-erased shadow.] The one-sorted membership structure obtained from the staged
two-sorted presentation by forgetting the explicit stage sort; see Definition~\ref{def:staged}.
\item[Assumption box.] The four named infinitary commitments
\textbf{C-INF}, \textbf{C-POW}, \textbf{C-REPL}, and \textbf{C-SEL}; see
\S\ref{ssec:box}. They are hypotheses, not conclusions.
\item[Strict theory extension.] A package change whose new object map does not factor through the
old ground object; in this paper it is instantiated by Theorem~\ref{thm:nonfactor}.
\item[Ground lens.] The countable ground model read through its coded reals
$\Sig_M=2^\omega\cap M$; see Definition~\ref{def:groundlens}.
\end{description}

\label{def:sau-nondescending-structure}
A promoted structure \(U\) is non-descending relative to \((q,I_B)\), written
\[
U\not\downarrow_q,
\]
when the declared lower interface cannot accept \(U\) as a lower-layer object, operation, or claim. In exact update profiles this means
\[
\delta^{\mathrm{split}}_1(q,U)\neq\varnothing.

\end{align*}

\label{def:sau-failure-fields}

\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp,\\
\{\star\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}

\[
F_{\mathrm{solve}}(\mathfrak C)=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P)
\text{ and }\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass},\\
\{\star\},&\text{otherwise},

\label{def:sau-basic-audit-grammar}
The basic SAU audit grammar \(\mathcal G_{\operatorname{Basic}}\) is the typed grammar whose primitive boundary constructors are the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Composite or power constructor:}
\[
C(U)=U^n\quad(n\ge2)
\]
or, more generally, a finite composite of a hidden update whose selected composite descends.
\item \textbf{Coefficient or standard-part constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\kappa(\Phi(U)),
\]
where \(\kappa\) is a coefficient, jet, residue, leading-term, or standard-part audit map.
\item \textbf{Projection or shadow constructor:}
\[
C(U)=q(U),
\]
where \(q\) is a declared shadow, real-part, observable, quotient, or forgetful projection.
\item \textbf{Invariant or fixed-point constructor:}
\[
C(U)\in \Inv_G(\mathcal T_1)\quad\text{or}\quad C(U)\in \operatorname{Fix}(G),
\]
where a promoted symmetry action makes the selected expression invariant and hence lower-descending.
\item \textbf{Trace, norm, or symmetric aggregation constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\sum_{g\in G}gU,
\qquad
C(U)=\prod_{g\in G}gU,
\]
or another declared finite symmetric aggregation of a promoted orbit.
\item \textbf{Quotient or obstruction-class constructor:}
\[
C(U)=[U]\in M/N,
\]
where \(N\) is the subobject declared exact, trivial, gauge, globally generated, or lower-null.
\end{enumerate}
The grammar is closed under finite products, finite sums, ordered tuples, and composition with already accepted lower-layer verifiers.  It is not closed under arbitrary informal analogy, undeclared semantic interpretation, or unaudited transfer.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:coh-period-audit}
A directed closed walk or cycle \(\gamma\) determines a signed sum of oriented edges.  For \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), define the period of \(a\) around \(\gamma\) by
\[
\oint_\gamma a
=
\sum_{e\in \gamma}\epsilon_e a(e),
\]
where \(\epsilon_e=1\) if \(\gamma\) traverses \(e\) in the chosen orientation and \(\epsilon_e=-1\) if it traverses \(e\) in the opposite orientation.  The period audit is the map
\[
\operatorname{Per}(a):Z_1(\Gamma;k)\to k,
\qquad
\operatorname{Per}(a)(\gamma)=\oint_\gamma a,
\]
where \(Z_1(\Gamma;k)\) is the cycle space of the graph.

source_wording_tex:
\label{def:coh-period-audit}
A directed closed walk or cycle \(\gamma\) determines a signed sum of oriented edges.  For \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), define the period of \(a\) around \(\gamma\) by
\[
\oint_\gamma a
=
\sum_{e\in \gamma}\epsilon_e a(e),
\]
where \(\epsilon_e=1\) if \(\gamma\) traverses \(e\) in the chosen orientation and \(\epsilon_e=-1\) if it traverses \(e\) in the opposite orientation.  The period audit is the map
\[
\Per(a):Z_1(\Gamma;k)\to k,
\qquad
\Per(a)(\gamma)=\oint_\gamma a,
\]
where \(Z_1(\Gamma;k)\) is the cycle space of the graph.

The canonical witness vector is the ordered family
\[
\mathfrak W_{4}
=
(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Imag}},\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Jet}},\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Gal}},\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Coh}}),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Imag}}\) is the root-composite witness built from the four-phase carrier \(C_4=\{1,i,-1,-i\}\), the real-shadow lens \(q:C_4\to\{-1,0,1\}\), the quarter-turn \(G(z)=iz\), and the descending square \(G^2\).
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Jet}}\) is the coefficient witness built from the dual-number algebra \(\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), the non-real nilpotent \(\varepsilon\), the first-jet expression \(f(x+\varepsilon)\), and the coefficient audit \([\varepsilon]f(x+\varepsilon)=f'(x)\).
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Gal}}\) is the invariant-descent witness built from a finite Galois splitting field \(L/K\), a non-descending root \(\alpha\notin K\), and descending invariant audits such as elementary symmetric functions, \(L^{\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)}=K\), \(\Tr_{L/K}\), and \(\Nm_{L/K}\).
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Coh}}\) is the obstruction-ledger witness built from a finite connected graph \(\Gamma\), local edge data \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), the global-potential descent question \(a=d_0\phi\), and the obstruction class \([a]\in H^1(\Gamma;k)\).
\end{enumerate}
Each component of \(\mathfrak W_4\) is understood with its declared lower problem profile, promotion bridge, audit channels, and nonclaim register from the corresponding theorem sheet.

\label{def:sau-canonical-profile-registry}
The four canonical witnesses determine the registry
\[
\mathcal R_4=
\{\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{RootComp}},\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{Coeff}},\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{InvDesc}},\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{ObsLed}}\},
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{RootComp}}\) is the root-composite profile:
\[
U\not\downarrow_q,
\qquad
U^n\downarrow_q F.
\]
\item \(\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{Coeff}}\) is the coefficient or standard-part profile:
\[
U\not\downarrow_{\mathcal T_0},
\qquad
\kappa(\Phi(U))=a^\sharp
\]
for a coefficient, standard-part, or jet audit \(\kappa\).
\item \(\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{InvDesc}}\) is the invariant-descent profile:
\[
U\notin \mathcal T_0,
\qquad
C(U)\in \operatorname{Inv}(\mathcal T_1/\mathcal T_0)\cong \mathcal T_0.
\]
\item \(\mathfrak p_{\mathsf{ObsLed}}\) is the obstruction-ledger profile:
\[
\text{local or partial data fails descent},
\qquad
[U]=0\iff\text{descent succeeds}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

\label{def:sau-strictness-defect}
Given object maps \(\pi_0:S\to O_0\) and \(\pi_1:S\to O_1\), define the factorization defect
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)

\{(s,s')\in S\times S:\pi_0(s)=\pi_0(s')\text{ and }\pi_1(s)\neq\pi_1(s')\}.

A role label is not a total algebraic generator. It is a typed channel whose activation requires role-aligned witness data, threshold data, level data, visibility data, audit data, and an explicit nonclaim record.

conclusion: An SAU certificate is exact-six when, in addition to Definition , the bridge record determines an inherited FATCD -style description D_B whose six role channels all have active projections: Status_i(D_B)=active_projection, pi_i(D_B)\ exists, i=1, ,6. Equivalently, the bridge record contains role-aligned active witness data for all six channels: (W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4,W_5,W_6), where: W_1 witnesses descent or descent obstruction; W_2 witnesses lower nonrepresentability and promoted representability; W_3 witnesses route, phase, orbit, path, or coherence data suppressed by the lower layer; W_4 witnesses the stage transition from lower layer to promoted layer and back to audited descent; W_5 witnesses packaging, quotienting, or completion; W_6 witnesses audit, provenance, replay, no-overreading, and nonclaims. Each witness must carry threshold, level, visibility, audit, and nonclaim records. Exact-six SAU is a scoped FATCD -anchored certificate type, not a claim that every useful mathematical extension activates all six channels.

\label{def:sau-basic-audit-grammar}
The basic SAU audit grammar \(\mathcal G_{\operatorname{Basic}}\) is the typed grammar whose primitive boundary constructors are the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Composite or power constructor:}
\[
C(U)=U^n\quad(n\ge2)
\]
or, more generally, a finite composite of a hidden update whose selected composite descends.
\item \textbf{Coefficient or standard-part constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\kappa(\Phi(U)),
\]
where \(\kappa\) is a coefficient, jet, residue, leading-term, or standard-part audit map.
\item \textbf{Projection or shadow constructor:}
\[
C(U)=q(U),
\]
where \(q\) is a declared shadow, real-part, observable, quotient, or forgetful projection.
\item \textbf{Invariant or fixed-point constructor:}
\[
C(U)\in \Inv_G(\mathcal T_1)\quad\text{or}\quad C(U)\in \operatorname{Fix}(G),
\]
where a promoted symmetry action makes the selected expression invariant and hence lower-descending.
\item \textbf{Trace, norm, or symmetric aggregation constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\sum_{g\in G}gU,
\qquad
C(U)=\prod_{g\in G}gU,
\]
or another declared finite symmetric aggregation of a promoted orbit.
\item \textbf{Quotient or obstruction-class constructor:}
\[
C(U)=[U]\in M/N,
\]
where \(N\) is the subobject declared exact, trivial, gauge, globally generated, or lower-null.
\end{enumerate}
The grammar is closed under finite products, finite sums, ordered tuples, and composition with already accepted lower-layer verifiers.  It is not closed under arbitrary informal analogy, undeclared semantic interpretation, or unaudited transfer.

\label{def:sau-basic-profile-registry}
The basic profile registry is
\[
\mathcal R_{\Basic}
=\{\RootComp,\Coeff,\ProjShad,\InvDesc,\AggInv,\ObsLed\}.
\]
The four canonical case-study profiles are the subregistry
\[
\mathcal R_{4}
=\{\RootComp,\Coeff,\InvDesc,\ObsLed\}.
\]
The registry map
\[
\rho_{\Basic}:\mathcal G_{\Basic}\longrightarrow\mathcal R_{\Basic}
\]
is defined on primitive heads by
\[
\rho_{\Basic}(U\mapsto U^n)=\RootComp,
\]
\[
\rho_{\Basic}(\kappa\circ\Phi)=\Coeff,
\]
\[
\rho_{\Basic}(q)=\ProjShad,
\]
\[
\rho_{\Basic}(\Inv_G\text{ or }\Fix(G))=\InvDesc,
\]
\[
\rho_{\Basic}(\sum_G,\prod_G,\text{symmetric aggregation})=\AggInv,
\]
\[
\rho_{\Basic}(U\mapsto[U]\in M/N)=\ObsLed.
\]
For composite boundary expressions, \(\rho_{\Basic}\) returns the finite ordered list or product of primitive profile labels appearing in the reduced expression.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:coh-period-audit}
A directed closed walk or cycle \(\gamma\) determines a signed sum of oriented edges.  For \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), define the period of \(a\) around \(\gamma\) by
\[
\oint_\gamma a
=
\sum_{e\in \gamma}\epsilon_e a(e),
\]
where \(\epsilon_e=1\) if \(\gamma\) traverses \(e\) in the chosen orientation and \(\epsilon_e=-1\) if it traverses \(e\) in the opposite orientation.  The period audit is the map
\[
\operatorname{Per}(a):Z_1(\Gamma;k)\to k,
\qquad
\operatorname{Per}(a)(\gamma)=\oint_\gamma a,
\]
where \(Z_1(\Gamma;k)\) is the cycle space of the graph.

conclusion: A computational substrate sigma is a typed bounded polynomial-time computation context . It consists of: an instance family X_ sigma ; a size function on instances together with a bound N_ sigma , so that only instances of size at most N_ sigma belong to the bounded carrier considered here; a declared solver-prefix family, assigning to each bounded instance the finite trace shape that a polynomial-time computation may generate before the history is audited. A substrate is therefore the typed context in which instances, scale, and trace formation have all been fixed, rather than a language or a set of inputs.

conclusion: Let sigma be a computational substrate. An autonomous lift on sigma is a typed object L=(gen_ L ,sigma_ L ,replay_ L ) with the following components: gen_ L is a deterministic polynomial-time history-generation procedure. In plain terms, it is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given the substrate input and the prior trace data, extends the computation history by one audited step. sigma_ L :H_ sigma ^ L → S is the internal-state readout of the lift, where S is the lift's finite typed state space. The value sigma_ L (h) records the internal determining state of the procedure at the history h . replay_ L is the all-input replay record for gen_ L : an audited machine-index and time-certificate object that allows the same polynomial-time procedure to be reproduced on any input. This is the audit-side bookkeeping supplied by the FATCD discipline . The autonomous lift is realized in Lean by the autonomous-lift declaration listed in ; the Lean record exposes additional family-characterizing predicates beyond the components named in the definition above. The narrowing-disclosure discipline is recorded in .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:autonomous-lift}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate.  An
\emph{autonomous lift} on \(\sigma\) is a typed object
\[
  L=(\mathrm{gen}_{L},\sigma_{L},\mathrm{replay}_{L})
\]
with the following components:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\mathrm{gen}_{L}\) is a deterministic polynomial-time
  history-generation procedure.  In plain terms, it is a deterministic
  polynomial-time algorithm that, given the substrate input and the
  prior trace data, extends the computation history by one audited
  step.
  \item \(\sigma_{L}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to S\) is the internal-state
  readout of the lift, where \(S\) is the lift's finite typed state
  space.  The value \(\sigma_{L}(h)\) records the internal determining
  state of the procedure at the history \(h\).
  \item \(\mathrm{replay}_{L}\) is the all-input replay record for
  \(\mathrm{gen}_{L}\): an audited machine-index and
  time-certificate object that allows the same polynomial-time
  procedure to be reproduced on any input.  This is the audit-side
  bookkeeping supplied by the \(\mathsf{FATCD}\) discipline
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsII2026}.\footnote{The autonomous lift is
  realized in Lean by the autonomous-lift declaration listed in
  \Cref{app:formalization}; the Lean record exposes additional
  family-characterizing predicates beyond the components named in the
  definition above.  The narrowing-disclosure discipline is recorded in
  \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\end{enumerate}

  history-generation procedure.  In plain terms, it is a deterministic
  polynomial-time algorithm that, given the substrate input and the
  prior trace data, extends the computation history by one audited
  step.
  \item \(\LiftState:\HistorySpace\to S\) is the internal-state
  readout of the lift, where \(S\) is the lift's finite typed state
  space.  The value \(\LiftState(h)\) records the internal determining
  state of the procedure at the history \(h\).
  \item \(\mathrm{replay}_{\Lift}\) is the all-input replay record for
  \(\mathrm{gen}_{\Lift}\): an audited machine-index and
  time-certificate object that allows the same polynomial-time
  procedure to be reproduced on any input.  This is the audit-side
  bookkeeping supplied by the \(\FATCD\) discipline
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsII2026}.\footnote{The autonomous lift is
  realized in Lean by the autonomous-lift declaration listed in
  \Cref{app:formalization}; the Lean record exposes additional
  family-characterizing predicates beyond the components named in the
  definition above.  The narrowing-disclosure discipline is recorded in
  \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:visibility-coupling}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate, let \(L\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\sigma\), and write
\(\sigma_{L}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to S\) for its internal-state readout.
The \emph{visibility coupling predicate}
\(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) holds if and only if there exist an
observable codomain \(\mathcal O\), a declared polynomial-time current
observable
\[
  \varphi_{Q}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to\mathcal O,
\]
and a polynomial-time function \(f:S\to\mathcal O\) such that
\[
  \bigl(\exists h,h'\inH_{\sigma}^{L},\,
      f(\sigma_{L}(h))\neq f(\sigma_{L}(h'))\bigr)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \bigl(\forall h\inH_{\sigma}^{L},\,
      \varphi_{Q}(h)=f(\sigma_{L}(h))\bigr).
\]

\label{def:xi:legal-energy-quotient}
The \emph{legal energy quotient} of \((E,C)\) is the orthogonal complement
\[
  E_C=(\Ker C)^\perp\subseteq E,
\]
together with the restricted audit form
\[
  C_0=C|_{E_C}>0
\]
which is strictly positive on \(E_C\).  The \emph{Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse}
\(C^\dagger\), following
\citet{Penrose1955GeneralizedInverse,BenIsraelGreville2003GeneralizedInverses},
acts as \(C_0^{-1}\) on \(E_C\) and as zero on \(\Ker C\).

This section gives the central object of the paper.  With the standing
hypotheses of \Cref{sec:setup} and the probe-family currency of
\Cref{sec:currency} in place, the joint native-dissolving currency matrix
decomposes into four blocks.  The adequacy residual is the Schur complement of
the native block
\citep{Schur1917Potenzreihen,Haynsworth1968Inertia,Albert1969PSDPartitioned,Cottle1974Manifestations,Zhang2005SchurApplications,HornJohnson2013MatrixAnalysis}:
the leftover content of the dissolving block after the native
block has explained as much as it can.

\begin{definition}[Native, dissolving, and joint block currencies]\label{def:xi:block-currencies}
Let \(L\colon E\to Y\) and \(D\colon E\to Z\) be null-legal probe families (in
the sense of \Cref{def:xi:null-legal-probe-family}), with restrictions
\(L_0,D_0\).  The \emph{native, dissolving, and cross currencies} are
\[
  K_{LL}=L_0C_0^{-1}L_0^*,
  \qquad
  K_{DL}=D_0C_0^{-1}L_0^*,
\]
\[
  K_{LD}=L_0C_0^{-1}D_0^*,
  \qquad
  K_{DD}=D_0C_0^{-1}D_0^*.
\]
Here \(K_{LL}=K_F\) for \(F=L\) and \(K_{DD}=K_F\) for \(F=D\) in the
probe-family currency of \Cref{def:xi:probe-family-currency}.  Equivalently,
\(K_{LL}\) and \(K_{DD}\) are positive semidefinite operators on \(Y\) and
\(Z\) respectively; \(K_{DL}\) and \(K_{LD}=K_{DL}^*\) are the corresponding
rectangular cross operators.  The \emph{joint currency matrix} of the combined
family \((L,D)\) is
\[
  K(D,L)
  =
  \begin{pmatrix}
    K_{LL} & K_{LD} \\
    K_{DL} & K_{DD}
  \end{pmatrix}.
\]
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:xi:extended-native-family}
Let \(M\colon E\to W\) be an additional null-legal native probe family.  The
\emph{extended native family} is
\[
  L^+
  =
  \begin{bmatrix}
    L\\
    M
  \end{bmatrix}
  \colon E\to Y\oplus W,
  \qquad
  L^+u=(Lu,Mu),
\]
which is null-legal because \(L\) and \(M\) both vanish on \(\Ker C\).  The
\emph{conditional native currency of \(M\) given \(L\)} is the Schur complement
\[
  K_{MM\mid L}
  =
  K_{MM}-K_{ML}K_{LL}^\dagger K_{LM},
\]
also known as the shorted operator of \(K_{MM}\) by the \(L\)-block
\citep{AndersonWN1971Shorted,AndersonTrapp1975ShortedII}.  The
\emph{conditional dissolving-extension cross currency} is
\[
  K_{DM\mid L}
  =
  K_{DM}-K_{DL}K_{LL}^\dagger K_{LM},
  \qquad
  K_{MD\mid L}=K_{DM\mid L}^*.
\]
The conditional joint currency block is positive semidefinite, so in
particular \(K_{MM\mid L}\succeq 0\) on \(W\); the rectangular cross
block \(K_{DM\mid L}\) is paired with its adjoint \(K_{MD\mid L}\).
\(K_{MM\mid L}\) vanishes precisely when the added probes \(M\) are
already explained by \(L\) on the legal quotient.

conclusion: An involutive object ledger is a tuple X=(X,J,mu,psi,Y, J), where: [label=( )] X is the visible object space; J:X→ X is an involution; mu is a positive object ledger measure, meaning a positive Radon-type measure on X , or a finite positive weight system on X ; Y is a real Hilbert response space; J:Y→ Y is a linear isometric involution; psi:X→ Y is an equivariant readout: psi(Jx)= Jpsi(x). Define P_-:= I- J 2 , psi_-(x):=P_-psi(x). Here P_- is the spectral projection onto the -1 -eigenspace of the isometric involution J , which is the standard anti-invariant decomposition for an involution on a Hilbert space . The anti-invariant object ledger is A_X:=∈t_X psi_-(x)psi_-(x)^* dmu(x), interpreted in the finite-rank or trace-class sense whenever required.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:main:involutive-ledger}
An involutive object ledger is a tuple
\[
  \mathfrak X=(X,J,\mu,\psi,Y,\mathcal J),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \(X\) is the visible object space;
\item \(J:X\to X\) is an involution;
\item \(\mu\) is a positive object ledger measure, meaning a positive
  Radon-type measure on \(X\), or a finite positive weight system on
  \(X\);
\item \(Y\) is a real Hilbert response space;
\item \(\mathcal J:Y\to Y\) is a linear isometric involution;
\item \(\psi:X\to Y\) is an equivariant readout:
\[
  \psi(Jx)=\mathcal J\psi(x).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Define
\[
  P_-:=\frac{I-\mathcal J}{2},\qquad \psi_-(x):=P_-\psi(x).
\]
Here \(P_-\) is the spectral projection onto the \(-1\)-eigenspace
of the isometric involution \(\mathcal J\), which is the standard
anti-invariant decomposition for an involution on a Hilbert space
\citep{Conway1990FunctionalAnalysis}.
The anti-invariant object ledger is
\[
  \mathsf A_X:=\int_X \psi_-(x)\psi_-(x)^*\,d\mu(x),
\]
interpreted in the finite-rank or trace-class sense whenever required.

conclusion: A candidate package counts as a promoted package on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold: [label=( )] Sufficiency. The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus. Induced closure. The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law. Second-stage stability. The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility. Control admissibility. The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way. No-smuggling. The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized. Slice legibility. On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:promoted-package-criterion}
A candidate package counts as a \emph{promoted package} on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Sufficiency.} The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus.
\item \textbf{Induced closure.} The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law.
\item \textbf{Second-stage stability.} The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility.
\item \textbf{Control admissibility.} The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way.
\item \textbf{No-smuggling.} The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized.
\item \textbf{Slice legibility.} On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.
\end{enumerate}

source_wording_tex:
\label{def:promoted-package-criterion}
A candidate package counts as a \emph{promoted package} on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Sufficiency.} The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus.
\item \textbf{Induced closure.} The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law.
\item \textbf{Second-stage stability.} The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility.
\item \textbf{Control admissibility.} The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way.
\item \textbf{No-smuggling.} The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized.
\item \textbf{Slice legibility.} On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: A distinct case occurs when promotion is available only after context or protocol state is internalized into the package. We call this protocol-indexed promotion. The base candidate does not qualify honestly on its own, because its apparent success depends on omitted protocol state, but an internalized or explicitly indexed version satisfies the promoted-package criterion once that dependence is represented inside the state object. This is stronger than a mere artifact diagnosis and weaker than intrinsic promotion: the route remains live, but only as an indexed package rather than as a context-free one.

conclusion: A reduction from C to D on the same surface Sigma is a map phi : X_ C → X_ D satisfying, for all admissible arguments, V_ C (x) implies V_ D (phi(x)), rho_ C (s, x) implies rho_ D (s, phi(x)), lambda_ C (x, o) implies lambda_ D (phi(x), o), tau_ C (g, x, y) implies tau_ D (g, phi(x), phi(y)). We write C D when a reduction exists, and say C is non-reducible among a family \ D_i\ _ i ∈ I if C D_i for every i . This is the C3 comparator of Section .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A \emph{reduction} from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{D}$ on the same surface $\Sigma$
is a map $\phi \colon X_{\mathcal{C}} \to X_{\mathcal{D}}$ satisfying, for all
admissible arguments,
\[
V_{\mathcal{C}}(x) \Rightarrow V_{\mathcal{D}}(\phi(x)), \qquad
\rho_{\mathcal{C}}(s, x) \Rightarrow \rho_{\mathcal{D}}(s, \phi(x)),
\]
\[
\lambda_{\mathcal{C}}(x, o) \Rightarrow \lambda_{\mathcal{D}}(\phi(x), o),
\qquad
\tau_{\mathcal{C}}(g, x, y) \Rightarrow \tau_{\mathcal{D}}(g, \phi(x), \phi(y)).
\]
We write $\mathcal{C} \preceq \mathcal{D}$ when a reduction exists, and say
$\mathcal{C}$ is \emph{non-reducible} among a family
$\{\mathcal{D}_i\}_{i \in I}$ if $\mathcal{C} \not\preceq \mathcal{D}_i$ for every
$i$. This is the C3 comparator of
Section~\ref{sec:candidate-classes-reductions-criteria}.

conclusion: This appendix collects the formal definitions and theorem statements used in the main text. At the level of general mathematical form, the quotient and factorization language used here sits near behavioral equivalence, bisimulation, exact aggregation, and standard quotient-factorization arguments . It does not reproduce proofs. The comparison base is inherited from the first three papers of the series: fixed support and admissibility, the current and predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. The present paper uses those inherited structures only to define and compare the flagship recombination family on a common exact-finite support. At the single-history level, the current quotient Q_i identifies reachable histories that are indistinguishable by the current event package, while the predictive quotient M_i identifies histories that remain indistinguishable under all admissible future generator/observable words on the reachable image. At the branch-assemblage level, the branchwise quotient K_i identifies assemblages with the same weighted multiset of predictive classes, while the recombination quotient R_i identifies assemblages that are indistinguishable by admissible later recombination observables. When recombination equivalence refines branchwise equivalence there is a canonical forgetful map _i : R_i → K_i .

conclusion: For the purposes of this paper, a reduction 2-complex associated to a rewriting system R consists of the following data. A set of 0 -cells, namely the states, words, or terms under consideration. A set of directed 1 -cells, namely the one-step rewrites x → y . A set of generating 2 -cells, each attached to a local two-route branching pattern with common source. In the finite-ARS setting these are local peaks. In the string and term-rewriting settings used in this paper, these are reachable critical pairs relative to the chosen start states and exploration bounds.

An \emph{admissible global realization} of an event package
\[
\mathfrak{E}=(\mathcal C,\{B_c\}_{c\in\mathcal C},\sim,\mathcal A)
\]
consists of a finite set \(\Omega\) and maps \(\pi_c:\Omega\to A_c\) for all \(c\in\mathcal C\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Context coverage.} For every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and every atom \(a\in A_c\), there exists \(\omega\in\Omega\) with \(\pi_c(\omega)=a\).
    \item \textbf{Event realization.} Each context event \(E\in B_c\) is realized by \(\mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} E \rrbracket_\Omega^c\subseteq \Omega\).
    \item \textbf{Shared-event consistency.} Whenever \(E\in B_c\), \(F\in B_d\), and \(E\sim F\), one has
    \[
    \mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} E \rrbracket_\Omega^c = \mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} F \rrbracket_\Omega^d.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Audit admissibility.} The realization respects the package discipline encoded in \(\mathcal A\): no unlicensed hidden distinctions are introduced, and the realization remains within the layer's admissible record and interface class.
\end{enumerate}

\label{def:duality_confinement:anti-invariant-ledger}
The \emph{anti-invariant object ledger} of \(\hat{\mathfrak{X}}\) is the positive
cone element
\[
  A_{X}
  :=
  \int_X \psi_{-}(x)\psi_{-}(x)^*\,d\mu(x),
  \qquad
  \psi_{-}(x)=P_{-}\psi(x).
\]
Equivalently, \(A_{X}\) is the Gram-type positive element generated
by integrating the anti-invariant readout against the object-ledger
measure \(\mu\).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:duality_confinement:separating-readout}
The anti-invariant readout \(\psi_{-}\) is
\emph{qualitatively separating} when, on the visible support of
\(\mu\),
\[
  \psi_{-}(x)=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  x\in\Fix(J).
\]
In the finite weighted case this means the equivalence holds for
every \(x\in X\) with positive weight.  In the measure-theoretic
case it means the equivalence holds outside a \(\mu\)-null set.

It is \emph{quantitatively separating} with modulus \(m\) when
\[
  m:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)
\]
and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) and every \(x\in X\),
\[
  \dist(x,\Fix(J))\geq\varepsilon
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \|\psi_{-}(x)\|\geq m(\varepsilon).
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:duality_confinement:completed-domination-bridge}
A \emph{completed domination bridge} from \(A_{X}\) to a
carrier-side anti-invariant currency \(K^{-}\) consists of a
positive defect \(E\) in the typed positive cone, with
\[
  0\preceq E,
\]
together with the domination relation
\[
  A_{X}\preceq K^{-}+E.
\]
The bridge is \emph{exact} when \(E=0\) and \emph{defected} when
the defect term is retained.  A sequence of bridges
\[
  A_{X}\preceq \Kminus_{n}+E_n
\]
is a \emph{domination-record sequence} when the associated positive
bounds
\[
  B_n=\Kminus_{n}+E_n
\]
satisfy
\[
  \trace B_n\to0
  \qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

\label{def:duality_confinement:completed-domination-bridge}
A \emph{completed domination bridge} from \(\AX\) to a
carrier-side anti-invariant currency \(\Kminus\) consists of a
positive defect \(E\) in the typed positive cone, with
\[
  0\preceq E,
\]
together with the domination relation
\[
  \AX\preceq \Kminus+E.
\]
The bridge is \emph{exact} when \(E=0\) and \emph{defected} when
the defect term is retained.  A sequence of bridges
\[
  \AX\preceq \Kminus_{n}+E_n
\]
is a \emph{domination-record sequence} when the associated positive
bounds
\[
  B_n=\Kminus_{n}+E_n
\]
satisfy
\[
  \trace B_n\to0
  \qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:duality_confinement:exhaustive-moving-ledger}
An \emph{exhaustive moving ledger} over an involutive object ledger
\(\hat{\mathfrak{X}}\) consists of a sequence of positive cone elements
\(A_{X,n}\), inclusion transports \(\iota_n\), and positive tails
\(T_n\) with \(0\preceq T_n\), such that, for every \(n\),
\[
  A_{X}\preceq \iota_n A_{X,n}\iota_n^*+T_n.
\]
It is \emph{vanishing-exhaustive} when there are positive bounds
\(B_n\) satisfying
\[
  A_{X,n}\preceq B_n
\]
and
\[
  \trace(\iota_n B_n\iota_n^*)+\trace T_n\to0
  \qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

\label{def:duality_confinement:defected-budget}
A \emph{defected obstruction budget} at level \(n\) is a domination
record of the form
\[
  A_{X}
  \preceq
  (1+t)\bigl(\Kminus_{n}+E_{\mathrm{src},n}\bigr)
  +(1+t^{-1})E_{\mathrm{br},n},
\]
where \(t>0\), where \(E_{\mathrm{src},n}\) is a source defect, and
where \(E_{\mathrm{br},n}\) is a bridge defect.  Both defects are
positive cone elements.  The unparameterized budget is obtained by
setting \(t=1\), which adds the two defect contributions without
optimization.

conclusion: A control space U is any set of variables over which macro-law feasibility is to be charted. A control point u ∈ U may include a microscopic law parameter, a packaging or lens, a staging depth tau , a protocol or mechanism variable, and a budget coordinate. Different atlases in this paper use different choices of U : law-space atlases vary microscopic law parameters while holding packaging fixed, packaging-space atlases vary the packaging while holding the microscopic law fixed, and mechanism-space atlases vary protocol/mechanism choices over a fixed finite-state substrate. For a given control point u , let x_t ∈ X denote the microscopic state and let x_ t+1 K_u( x_t) denote the corresponding microscopic update law. Let tau(u) ∈ N be the staging depth at which the macro-description is assessed. An admissible macro-description at u is a pair (Pi,L) ∈ C(u) , where Pi : X → Y is a packaging map and L is a candidate macro update rule on Y . The family C(u) collects whichever package/law pairs are allowed at that control point.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:control_space}
A \emph{control space} $\mathcal{U}$ is any set of variables over which macro-law feasibility is to be charted. A control point $u \in \mathcal{U}$ may include a microscopic law parameter, a packaging or lens, a staging depth $\tau$, a protocol or mechanism variable, and a budget coordinate. Different atlases in this paper use different choices of $\mathcal{U}$: law-space atlases vary microscopic law parameters while holding packaging fixed, packaging-space atlases vary the packaging while holding the microscopic law fixed, and mechanism-space atlases vary protocol/mechanism choices over a fixed finite-state substrate.

For a given control point $u$, let $x_t \in X$ denote the microscopic state and let
\[
x_{t+1} \sim K_u(\,\cdot \mid x_t)
\]
denote the corresponding microscopic update law. Let $\tau(u) \in \mathbb{N}$ be the staging depth at which the macro-description is assessed. An \emph{admissible macro-description} at $u$ is a pair $(\Pi,L) \in \mathfrak{C}(u)$, where $\Pi : X \to Y$ is a packaging map and $L$ is a candidate macro update rule on $Y$. The family $\mathfrak{C}(u)$ collects whichever package/law pairs are allowed at that control point.

conclusion: A substrate S consists of: (i) a state carrier Z (finite in our canonical machine model), (ii) a composable dynamics primitive (autonomous in the canonical model), and (iii) an admissible family of deterministic observational maps (lenses) from Z to coarser description spaces. Additional internal structure may be present (e.g.\ registers, ledgers, prototype selectors), but must be represented as part of state or as derived operators.

\label{def:substrate}
A substrate $\mathcal S$ consists of:
(i) a state carrier $Z$ (finite in our canonical machine model),
(ii) a composable dynamics primitive (autonomous in the canonical model),
and (iii) an admissible family of deterministic observational maps (lenses) from $Z$ to coarser description spaces.
Additional internal structure may be present (e.g.\ registers, ledgers, prototype selectors), but must be represented as part of state or as derived operators.

conclusion: A carrier is a finite set X of states. A transition/action family over X is a finite set A of actions with, for each a∈ A , either a map F_a : X → X or a row-stochastic kernel P_a on X ; whether dynamics are deterministic or stochastic is declared per construction. A lens (observation map) is a map q : X → Y onto a finite value set; its fibers form the observational partition Pi_q of X . A policy for q is a feedback rule that selects actions measurably with respect to Pi_q (more generally, with respect to the history of q -values).

conclusion: A partition Pi' refines Pi when every block of Pi' is contained in a block of Pi . Given two lenses pi_0, pi_1 on the same carrier, the factorization defect is Delta_ fact (pi_0,pi_1) = \ (s,s') : pi_0(s)=pi_0(s') and pi_1(s)≠pi_1(s')\ , the set of split pairs: pairs identified by the coarse description and separated by the fine one. pi_1 factors through pi_0 (there is with pi_1= pi_0 ) if and only if Delta_ fact (pi_0,pi_1)=∅ . A nonempty defect is the exact, checkable meaning of ``the fine content is not recoverable from the coarse description'' used throughout this paper.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A partition $\Pi'$ \emph{refines} $\Pi$ when every block of $\Pi'$ is contained
in a block of $\Pi$. Given two lenses $\pi_0, \pi_1$ on the same carrier, the
\emph{factorization defect} is
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1) \;=\; \{(s,s') : \pi_0(s)=\pi_0(s') \text{ and }

conclusion: Fix a carrier with declared dynamics and a lens q . Two states (or histories) are observationally equivalent when all admissible current observables agree on them; the induced quotient is the current public quotient Q . They are predictively equivalent when they agree on the full family of admissible future behavior (continuation laws, or distributions over future observable trajectories under all admissible continuations); the induced quotient is the predictive quotient M . Predictive equivalence refines observational equivalence, giving a canonical comparison map pi : M → Q . The gap between them, same Q -class with different M -class, is a factorization defect and is the recurring engine of this paper.

The viability kernel K_ viab is the greatest fixed point of the controlled-invariance operator V(K) = \ s ∈ K : s safe and a ∈ A_ feas (s) with Post(s,a) ⊆ K \ , computed by descending iteration; this is the standard discrete-time viability kernel . For a lens , we write K_ viab ( ) for the best kernel achievable by -measurable policies. A nonempty kernel means controlled persistence in the model, nothing more.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Fix a carrier $X$, a safety predicate, feasible action sets, and declared
successor supports. The \emph{viability kernel} $K_{\mathrm{viab}}$ is the greatest fixed
point of the controlled-invariance operator
\[
V(K) = \{\, s \in K : s \text{ safe and } \exists a \in A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s)
\text{ with } \mathrm{Post}(s,a) \subseteq K \,\},
\]
computed by descending iteration; this is the standard discrete-time viability
kernel \citep{AnayaEtAl2009Viability, AubinBayenSaintPierre2011}. For a lens
$\ell$, we write $K_{\mathrm{viab}}(\ell)$ for the best kernel achievable by
$\ell$-measurable policies. A nonempty kernel means controlled persistence in
the model, nothing more.

conclusion: The full C-package C is the eight-clause full-design and audit contract C1 – C8 , together with cross-clause coherence data and a full promotion-gate panel. A candidate consists of a carrier X , declared transition/action families, a public lens and exposure channels, a predictive self-lens, branch structure, a maintenance ledger, and protocol generators; the clauses constrain that data as follows. A declared multiscale exposure-closure family with robust fixed-point structure: closure operators E_tau at declared stagings tau , exact fixed-point and defect bookkeeping, and perturbation audits with declared retention thresholds. A strict promoted distinction across declared layers: Delta_ fact (pi_0,pi_1)≠∅ for the declared lower and promoted readouts, certified by a split pair. A recursively stable self-coordinate: refinement of the public self-lens by dynamical profiles terminates at a predictive quotient that carries the package's own continuation coordinate. The determining predictive state is not exposed relative to the declared public channel family: no admissible current observable factors through it non-constantly on the realized support. Hiddenness is channel-relative by construction. A declared audit of action credit: generator provenance routes computed directionality into self, other, or none, with scheduled and internalized controls that must not be credited as self. A maintained, funded order/tick/arrow structure: a staged phase carrier that persists and progresses under budget, with the arrow carried by the package's own audit channel rather than by external scheduling. Nonempty maintained viability: K_ viab ≠∅ under the declared maintenance ledger, with underfunding collapsing the kernel.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:cpackage}
The \emph{full C-package} $\mathfrak{C}$ is the eight-clause full-design and audit
contract $\mathrm{C1}$--$\mathrm{C8}$, together with cross-clause coherence
data and a full promotion-gate panel. A candidate consists of a carrier $X$,
declared transition/action families, a public lens and exposure channels, a
predictive self-lens, branch structure, a maintenance ledger, and protocol
generators; the clauses constrain that data as follows.
\begin{description}
\item[C1 (objecthood).] A declared multiscale exposure-closure family with
robust fixed-point structure: closure operators $E_\tau$ at declared stagings
$\tau$, exact fixed-point and defect bookkeeping, and perturbation audits with
declared retention thresholds.
\item[C2 (strict promotion).] A strict promoted distinction across declared
layers: $\Delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\emptyset$ for the declared lower and promoted
readouts, certified by a split pair.
\item[C3 (reflexive self-coordinate).] A recursively stable self-coordinate:
refinement of the public self-lens by dynamical profiles terminates at a
predictive quotient that carries the package's own continuation coordinate.
\item[C4 (non-exposure).] The determining predictive state is not exposed
relative to the declared public channel family: no admissible current
observable factors through it non-constantly on the realized support.
Hiddenness is channel-relative by construction.
\item[C5 (drive/credit).] A declared audit of action credit: generator
provenance routes computed directionality into \emph{self}, \emph{other}, or
\emph{none}, with scheduled and internalized controls that must not be
credited as self.
\item[C6 (temporal closure).] A maintained, funded order/tick/arrow structure:
a staged phase carrier that persists and progresses under budget, with the
arrow carried by the package's own audit channel rather than by external
scheduling.
\item[C7 (binding).] Strict recombination refinement over the branchwise
quotient: joint content over declared branches, witnessed by
$R_{\mathrm{rec}} \succ K_{\mathrm{bw}}$ (Section~\ref{sec:structure}).
\item[C8 (viability).] Nonempty maintained viability: $K_{\mathrm{viab}}\neq\emptyset$
under the declared maintenance ledger, with underfunding collapsing the
kernel.
\end{description}

conclusion: The carrier is Z = P × W with |P|=6 public positions and |W|=2 hidden phases, so N = |Z| = 12 . The public self-lens is q(p,w)=p : the system can observe its own position but not its phase. The dynamics contain a live, unobserved phase slip with exact branch weights 3/4 and 1/4 , placed so that public history does not reconstruct the phase: the public trace (1,2,1) can end in either phase. A deadline makes the hidden phase viability-relevant: continuation beyond the deadline requires acting on the phase-dependent continuation law, and a wrong commitment exits the safe set.

conclusion: A controlled stochastic kernel is a row-stochastic tensor P[a,s,s'] Pr(s_ t+1 =s' s_t=s, a_t=a), with P[a,s,s'] 0 and _ s' P[a,s,s']=1 for all (a,s) . For a state distribution d (row vector), one step under action a is d' = d P[a, , ] .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Let $S=\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ be a finite state space and $A=\{0,1,\dots,m-1\}$ a finite action set. A controlled stochastic kernel is a row-stochastic tensor
\[
P[a,s,s'] \equiv \Pr(s_{t+1}=s' \mid s_t=s, a_t=a),
\]
with $P[a,s,s']\ge 0$ and $\sum_{s'}P[a,s,s']=1$ for all $(a,s)$. For a state distribution $d$ (row vector), one step under action $a$ is $d' = d\,P[a,\cdot,\cdot]$.

conclusion: Definition (Viability operator / controlled-invariance map). Given a candidate set K⊆ S , define the contracting controlled-invariance operator V(K) := Bigl\ s∈ K : Safe(s)\ \ a∈ A_ feas (s)\ s.t.\ Post(s,a)⊆ K Bigr\ . Intuitively: s remains in K if it is safe and there exists a feasible action whose entire successor support stays inside K . The explicit condition s∈ K makes V pointwise contracting ( V(K)⊆ K ), matching the standard ``greatest controlled-invariant subset'' construction and the assumptions of our Lean fixed-point anchor.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (Viability operator / controlled-invariance map).}
Given a candidate set $K\subseteq S$, define the contracting controlled-invariance operator
\[
\mathcal{V}(K) \;:=\; \Bigl\{\, s\in K \;:\; \mathrm{Safe}(s)\ \wedge\ \exists a\in A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s)\ \text{s.t.}\ \mathrm{Post}(s,a)\subseteq K \Bigr\}.
\]
Intuitively: $s$ remains in $K$ if it is safe and there exists a feasible action whose entire successor support stays inside $K$. The explicit condition $s\in K$ makes $\mathcal{V}$ pointwise contracting ($\mathcal{V}(K)\subseteq K$), matching the standard ``greatest controlled-invariant subset'' construction and the assumptions of our Lean fixed-point anchor.

conclusion: Definition (Action-sequence channel). Fix an initial state s_0 and a horizon H 1 . For an action sequence alpha=(a_0, ,a_ H-1 ) , let S_H be the random state after rolling out the kernel under alpha , and define Y=f(S_H) . expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (Action-sequence channel).}
Fix an initial state $s_0$ and a horizon $H\ge 1$. For an action sequence $\alpha=(a_0,\dots,a_{H-1})$, let $S_H$ be the random state after rolling out the kernel under $\alpha$, and define $Y=f(S_H)$. The induced channel from sequences to outputs is
\[
W[\alpha, y] \;:=\; \Pr(Y=y \mid s_0,\alpha).
\]
Equivalently, each row of $W$ is the output distribution obtained by propagating $\delta_{s_0}$ through the sequence and aggregating probability mass by $f$.

\paragraph{Definition (Action-sequence channel).}
Fix an initial state $s_0$ and a horizon $H\ge 1$. For an action sequence $\alpha=(a_0,\dots,a_{H-1})$, let $S_H$ be the random state after rolling out the kernel under $\alpha$, and define $Y=f(S_H)$. The induced channel from sequences to outputs is
\[
W[\alpha, y] \;:=\; \Pr(Y=y \mid s_0,\alpha).
\]
Equivalently, each row of $W$ is the output distribution obtained by propagating $\delta_{s_0}$ through the sequence and aggregating probability mass by $f$.

For a fixed $(s_0,H,f)$, empowerment is the channel capacity of $W$ \citep{klyubin2005,shannon1948}:
\[
\mathrm{Emp}(s_0;H,f) \;:=\; \max_{p(\alpha)} I(\mathcal{A};Y),
\]
where $\mathcal{A}$ is the chosen action-sequence random variable and $I(\cdot;\cdot)$ is mutual information \citep{shannon1948}. We compute this exactly (for small channels) via Blahut--Arimoto \citep{blahut1972,arimoto1972}.

\paragraph{Definition (Feasible empowerment).}
To respect P$_2$/P$_6$, we restrict the sequence set by ledger feasibility. Given costs $c(a)$ and budget $r(s_0)$, a sequence $\alpha$ is feasible if $\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} c(a_t) \le r(s_0)$. Feasible empowerment is the capacity of the restricted channel:
\[
\Emp_{\mathrm{feas}}(s_0;H,f) \;:=\; \mathrm{Cap}\bigl(W\ \text{restricted to feasible }\alpha\bigr).
\]
\paragraph{Remark (what ``feasible'' means in this paper).}
In principle, feasibility can be state- and branch-dependent because the ledger is part of the state and may evolve over the horizon. In this paper we use a deliberately simple, explicit notion: we treat the channel input alphabet as \emph{open-loop} action sequences and restrict it by an \emph{initial-budget} gate, i.e.\ $\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} c(a_t)\le r(s_0)$. This yields an ``open-loop budgeted empowerment'' that is easy to audit and compare under matched controls. It can over- or under-approximate stricter stepwise feasibility in settings with replenishment or branch-dependent constraints; we therefore treat it as an operational proxy and include calibrated nulls (Section~\ref{sec:ex_nulls}) to guard against mis-typed control channels.

conclusion: Definition (Empirical packaging endomap). Fix a horizon tau 0 and a stationary policy mu(a s) (deterministic or stochastic). For each macro label x , initialize a reference micro-distribution d_0 that is uniform over S_x . Let T_mu be the induced one-step transition under mu : T_mu := _ a∈ A mu(a s) P[a,s,s']. Evolve d_tau := d_0 T_mu^tau , aggregate to a macro distribution over X via pi , and define E(x) as the mode macro label at time tau (ties broken deterministically by smallest label). The resulting map E: X→ X is an empirical packaging endomap: it says ``starting from macro label x (with hidden microstate randomized), what macro label do we typically return to after tau steps under the policy?''

\paragraph{Definition (Empirical packaging endomap).}
Fix a horizon $\tau\ge 0$ and a stationary policy $\mu(a\mid s)$ (deterministic or stochastic). For each macro label $x$, initialize a reference micro-distribution $d_0$ that is uniform over $S_x$. Let $T_\mu$ be the induced one-step transition under $\mu$:
\[
T_\mu[s,s'] := \sum_{a\in A} \mu(a\mid s)\,P[a,s,s'].
\]
Evolve $d_\tau := d_0\,T_\mu^\tau$, aggregate to a macro distribution over $X$ via $\pi$, and define $E(x)$ as the mode macro label at time $\tau$ (ties broken deterministically by smallest label). The resulting map
\[
E: X\to X
\]
is an empirical \emph{packaging endomap}: it says ``starting from macro label $x$ (with hidden microstate randomized), what macro label do we typically return to after $\tau$ steps under the policy?''

\paragraph{Definition (Idempotence defect).}
The idempotence defect of $E$ is
\[
\mathrm{Def}(E) \;:=\; \frac{|\{x\in X: E(E(x))\neq E(x)\}|}{|X|}.
\]
If $\mathrm{Def}(E)\approx 0$, the macro labels behave like stable objects under the lens $\pi$ and the policy $\mu$; if $\mathrm{Def}(E)$ is large, the lens fails to induce objecthood (labels do not compose stably).

source_wording_tex:
The idempotence defect of $E$ is
\[
\mathrm{Def}(E) \;:=\; \frac{|\{x\in X: E(E(x))\neq E(x)\}|}{|X|}.
\]
If $\mathrm{Def}(E)\approx 0$, the macro labels behave like stable objects under the lens $\pi$ and the policy $\mu$; if $\mathrm{Def}(E)$ is large, the lens fails to induce objecthood (labels do not compose stably).

conclusion: A typed audited layer is a pair Tlayer i =(Xspace i , i ), where Xspace i is a finite microstate space and i :Xspace i →Xspace i is an idempotent self-map, i i = i . The induced equivalence relation on Xspace i identifies two microstates when they lie in the same pre-image of a fixed point in the image of i . Equivalently, the quotient partition is the partition of Xspace i into fibers of the map onto its fixed-point image .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A typed audited layer is a pair
\[
\Tlayer{i}=(\Xspace{i},\opmap{i}),
\]
where \(\Xspace{i}\) is a finite microstate space and \(\opmap{i}:\Xspace{i}\to\Xspace{i}\) is an idempotent self-map,
\[
\opmap{i}\circ\opmap{i}=\opmap{i}.
\]
The induced equivalence relation on \(\Xspace{i}\) identifies two microstates when they lie in the same pre-image of a fixed point in the image of \(\opmap{i}\). Equivalently, the quotient partition is the partition of \(\Xspace{i}\) into fibers of the map onto its fixed-point image \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}.

conclusion: Given a layer Tlayer i and a declared lookahead tau , the closure-deficit statistic CD_ tau is the conditional-information residual measuring how much next- tau -token structure on Xspace i remains unresolved by the quotient map i . Schematically, for an observed current microstate X_0 and a future window X_ >0, tau , CD_ tau H (X_ >0, tau i (X_0) ) - H (X_ >0, tau X_0 ). Thus CD_ tau is the conditional-entropy gap between prediction from the layer quotient and prediction from the raw microstate, restricted to the declared lookahead window. The runtime estimates this quantity from finite samples and reports estimator-quality flags alongside the value .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Given a layer \(\Tlayer{i}\) and a declared lookahead \(\tau\), the closure-deficit statistic \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\) is the conditional-information residual measuring how much next-\(\tau\)-token structure on \(\Xspace{i}\) remains unresolved by the quotient map \(\opmap{i}\). Schematically, for an observed current microstate \(X_0\) and a future window \(X_{>0,\le \tau}\),
\[
\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}
\;\approx\;
H\!\left(X_{>0,\le \tau}\mid \opmap{i}(X_0)\right)
-
H\!\left(X_{>0,\le \tau}\mid X_0\right).
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\) is the conditional-entropy gap between prediction from the layer quotient and prediction from the raw microstate, restricted to the declared lookahead window. The runtime estimates this quantity from finite samples and reports estimator-quality flags alongside the value \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}.

conclusion: Given a layer Tlayer i , lookahead tau , and readout f , the idempotence/self-consistency defect delta_ tau,f is the empirical fixed-point gap measuring deviation from i i = i on observed data through f . A typical estimator is a total-variation or analogous distributional distance between the empirical readout distribution after one application of i and after two applications: delta_ tau,f d (f( i (X_0)), f( i ( i (X_0))) ), with the future window and readout determining which empirical events are compared. As with CD_ tau , the runtime reports finite-sample support and propagates estimator-quality flags rather than treating small empirical deviations as exact equalities .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Given a layer \(\Tlayer{i}\), lookahead \(\tau\), and readout \(f\), the idempotence/self-consistency defect \(\delta_{\tau,f}\) is the empirical fixed-point gap measuring deviation from \(\opmap{i}\circ\opmap{i}=\opmap{i}\) on observed data through \(f\). A typical estimator is a total-variation or analogous distributional distance between the empirical readout distribution after one application of \(\opmap{i}\) and after two applications:
\[
\delta_{\tau,f}
\;\approx\;
d\!\left(f(\opmap{i}(X_0)),\, f(\opmap{i}(\opmap{i}(X_0)))\right),
\]
with the future window and readout determining which empirical events are compared. As with \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\), the runtime reports finite-sample support and propagates estimator-quality flags rather than treating small empirical deviations as exact equalities \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}.

conclusion: Let q_i(s)= i (s) denote the parent quotient representative for a parent layer Tlayer i , and let q_ i+1 denote the candidate quotient evaluated on the same observed support through the declared candidate lift into Xspace i+1 . A candidate layer Tlayer i+1 is a strict extension of Tlayer i when there exist observed microstates s,s'∈ Xspace i such that q_i(s)=q_i(s') and q_ i+1 (s) q_ i+1 (s'). Equivalently, the candidate quotient does not factor through the parent quotient: it separates at least one pair that the parent identifies. The strict-extension certificate StrictExtCert records such a witness pair together with the audit evidence that licenses committing the candidate as a new layer .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Let \(q_i(s)=\opmap{i}(s)\) denote the parent quotient representative for a parent layer \(\Tlayer{i}\), and let \(q_{i+1}\) denote the candidate quotient evaluated on the same observed support through the declared candidate lift into \(\Xspace{i+1}\). A candidate layer \(\Tlayer{i+1}\) is a strict extension of \(\Tlayer{i}\) when there exist observed microstates \(s,s'\in \Xspace{i}\) such that
\[
q_i(s)=q_i(s')
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
q_{i+1}(s)\ne q_{i+1}(s').
\]
Equivalently, the candidate quotient does not factor through the parent quotient: it separates at least one pair that the parent identifies. The strict-extension certificate \(\mathsf{StrictExtCert}\) records such a witness pair together with the audit evidence that licenses committing the candidate as a new layer \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}.

conclusion: A stage game g is a declared two-player 2×2 game with action sets Act_i=\ C,D\ , joint-profile set Omega=Act_1×Act_2=\ CC,CD,DC,DD\ , and exact rational payoff map u_g:Omega→ Q^2 . A deterministic memory-one reactive rule is r=(alpha,r_ CC ,r_ CD ,r_ DC ,r_ DD )∈\ C,D\ ^5, where alpha is the initial action and r_omega is the action after the previous joint profile omega∈Omega . The catalog R_ 32 contains all 2^5=32 such rules; named rules such as always-cooperate, always-defect, tit-for-tat, grim, and win-stay-lose-shift are catalog entries.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{description}
\item[Stage games.]
A stage game \(g\) is a declared two-player \(2\times2\) game with action sets
\(\Act_i=\{C,D\}\), joint-profile set
\(\ensuremath{\Omega}=\Act_1\times\Act_2=\{CC,CD,DC,DD\}\), and exact rational payoff
map \(u_g:\ensuremath{\Omega}\to\mathbb Q^2\).

\item[Memory-one rules.]
A deterministic memory-one reactive rule is
\[
  r=(\alpha,r_{CC},r_{CD},r_{DC},r_{DD})\in\{C,D\}^5,
\]
where \(\alpha\) is the initial action and \(r_\omega\) is the action after
the previous joint profile \(\omega\in\ensuremath{\Omega}\).  The catalog \(\ensuremath{\mathcal R_{32}}\)
contains all \(2^5=32\) such rules; named rules such as always-cooperate,
always-defect, tit-for-tat, grim, and win-stay-lose-shift are catalog entries.
