The non- X -equivalent\ state says that the residual closure of C is logically equivalent to some conjectural content X' distinct from X . The three carrier-residual equivalent states are CRE-TE , the target-equivalent fallback; CRE-BF , the bridge-failed dead end; and CRE-CTMT , the cascade-terminal matrix-element case. The last three are the three typed foreclosure modes available once the residual closure is X -equivalent. Equivalently, writing B for the accepted-imports base, non- X -equivalent_X(C) Longleftrightarrow X'. (R_C=0 X') X'≠ X, OpenPending_ B (X') Longleftrightarrow B(X'), NativeOutcome_ B (C,X') Longleftrightarrow ( B(X') R_C=0) OpenPending_ B (X'), CRE-TE _X(C) Longleftrightarrow (R_C=0 X) SelfAuditFail(C), CRE-BF _X(C) Longleftrightarrow NoBridge(C,X) BridgeMismatch(C,X), CRE-CTMT _X(C) Longleftrightarrow MRed(C) (C) (C,X).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:four-typed-states}
For a typed primary carrier \(C\) aimed at \(X\), the four Part I
states are the following.  The non-$X$-equivalent\ state says that the
residual closure of \(C\) is logically equivalent to some conjectural
content \(X'\) distinct from \(X\).  The three carrier-residual
equivalent states are \textsc{CRE-TE}, the target-equivalent fallback;
\textsc{CRE-BF}, the bridge-failed dead end; and \textsc{CRE-CTMT}, the
cascade-terminal matrix-element case.  The last three are the
three typed foreclosure modes available once the residual closure is
$X$-equivalent.
Equivalently, writing \(\mathcal B\) for the accepted-imports base,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \exists X'.\, (R_C=0\leftrightarrow X')\wedge X'\neq X,\\
  \operatorname{OpenPending}_{\mathcal B}(X')
    &\Longleftrightarrow \neg \mathcal B(X'),\\
  \operatorname{NativeOutcome}_{\mathcal B}(C,X')
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      (\mathcal B(X')\wedge R_C=0)\vee
      \operatorname{OpenPending}_{\mathcal B}(X'),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      (R_C=0\leftrightarrow X)\wedge
      \operatorname{SelfAuditFail}(C),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \operatorname{NoBridge}(C,X)\vee
      \operatorname{BridgeMismatch}(C,X),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \operatorname{MRed}(C)\wedge
      \neg\operatorname{IRDec}(C)\wedge
      \neg\operatorname{MDEqTarget}(C,X).
\end{aligned}
\]

conclusion: The three-option derivation sweep is the Stage-6 sub-procedure that runs a trace-state-only closure attempt against three options. The framework-primitive option\ asks whether the closure is reachable by framework-primitive descent. The V-Differential elevation option\ asks whether elevating the data inside V-Differential resolves the closure route.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:four-axis-profile}
The four-axis calibration profile of a calibration consists of its algebraic identities,
detector class, descent invariants, and carrier orientation.  A candidate
calibration is a rebadge of an existing calibration when the two profiles
match on all four axes.  It is genuinely new relative to a family when it
is not a rebadge of any existing family member.
Thus a profile is the product
\[
  \mathsf{Profile}
  =
  \mathsf{AlgId}\times
  \mathsf{DetectorClass}\times
  \mathsf{DescentInv}\times
  \mathsf{CarrierOrient}.
\]
For profiles \(p\) and \(q\),
\[
  \mathsf{Rebadge}(p,q)
  \iff
  p_{\mathsf{alg}}=q_{\mathsf{alg}}\wedge
  p_{\mathsf{det}}=q_{\mathsf{det}}\wedge
  p_{\mathsf{desc}}=q_{\mathsf{desc}}\wedge
  p_{\mathsf{orient}}=q_{\mathsf{orient}},
\]
and
\[
  \mathsf{GenuineNew}(p,\mathcal F)
  \iff
  \forall q\in\mathcal F,\ \neg\mathsf{Rebadge}(p,q).
\]

conclusion: A framework-type is a four-axis record consisting of uniformity, worst-caseness, scoping, and packaging. On the P versus NP track, the cascade framework-type is nonuniform, average-case, scoped, and package-based. The standard Clay target framework-type is uniform, worst-case, unconditional, and language-based. The uniform / nonuniform and worst-case / average-case axes are the framework-type analogues of the distinctions surveyed in . Thus framework-type = Uniformity× WorstCaseness× Scoping× Packaging. For the P versus NP row, F_ PvNP = (nonuniform,averageCase, scoped,packageBased), T_ Clay = (uniform,worstCase, unconditional,languageBased). The matching predicate is componentwise equality on these four axes.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:framework-type}
A framework-type is a four-axis record consisting of uniformity,
worst-caseness, scoping, and packaging.  On the \(P\) versus \(NP\)
track, the cascade framework-type is nonuniform, average-case, scoped,
and package-based.  The standard Clay target framework-type is uniform,
worst-case, unconditional, and language-based.  The uniform /
nonuniform and worst-case / average-case axes are the framework-type
analogues of the distinctions surveyed in \cite{Impagliazzo1995FiveWorlds}.
Thus
\[
  framework-type
  =
  \mathsf{Uniformity}\times
  \mathsf{WorstCaseness}\times
  \mathsf{Scoping}\times
  \mathsf{Packaging}.
\]
For the \(P\) versus \(NP\) row,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  F_{\mathrm{PvNP}}
  &=
  (\mathsf{nonuniform},\mathsf{averageCase},
    \mathsf{scoped},\mathsf{packageBased}),\\
  T_{\mathrm{Clay}}
  &=
  (\mathsf{uniform},\mathsf{worstCase},
    \mathsf{unconditional},\mathsf{languageBased}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The matching predicate is componentwise equality on these four axes.

conclusion: A candidate current observable on H^ ! _ SAT is lawful when it satisfies the following five clauses. Machine indexing. The observable is realized by a declared deterministic polynomial-time transducer drawn from K_ poly , with an associated machine index. Time certificate. The transducer carries a polynomial time certificate in the input length, witnessed by an explicit polynomial. All-input replay convention. The observable is defined on every encoded SAT instance admitted at the current stage, with a replay convention for the corresponding all-input transcript. Visibility bookkeeping. \label{def:pvnp:lawfulness-discipline}
A candidate current observable on \(H^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) is \emph{lawful} when it
satisfies the following five clauses.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Machine indexing.}  The observable is realized by a
  declared deterministic polynomial-time transducer drawn from
  \(K_{\mathrm{poly}}\), with an associated machine index.
  \item \emph{Time certificate.}  The transducer carries a polynomial
  time certificate in the input length, witnessed by an explicit
  polynomial.
  \item \emph{All-input replay convention.}  The observable is defined
  on every encoded SAT instance admitted at the current stage, with a
  replay convention for the corresponding all-input transcript.
  \item \emph{Visibility bookkeeping.}  The observable reads only the
  declared \(Q\)-visible projection of the history, as selected by the
  visibility lens of \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\).
  \item \emph{No-smuggling records.}  The observable carries explicit
  audit records satisfying the gate predicates declared in the audit
  interface.
\end{enumerate}

\label{def:pvnp:omega-sat}
The \emph{autonomous lift} \(\OmegaSAT\) on the saturated SAT layer is
the deterministic-policy record consisting of:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item a SAT-specific lift-state space, whose elements encode the
  internal state of the autonomous policy as it generates SAT
  histories;
  \item an update rule sending a current lift state, active encoded
  SAT instance, and audited-shell bookkeeping data to the next lift
  state;
  \item a history-generation link sending lift-state trajectories to
  the corresponding histories in \(\Hsat\);
  \item a continuation catalog assigning to each lift state the
  admissible witness-side and predictive continuations available from
  that state.
\end{enumerate}
\footnote{The autonomous lift is realized in Lean by the autonomous
lift declaration listed in \Cref{app:formalization}, with the policy
components \((\OmegaSAT\)-state, update rule, history-generation map,
continuation catalog) exposed as independent fields together with
Prop-level no-oracle / no-hidden-witness commitments.  The
deterministic-policy linkage between the update rule and the
history-generation map is recorded paper-side.  See
\Cref{app:formalization} for the narrowing-disclosure discipline.}

        self-reduction route used in Translation Theorem~B.

\label{def:pvnp:aor-instance:object}
Let \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{PvNP}}\) be the SAT scope consisting of the
saturated SAT layer \(\Tsat\), the lawful polynomial-time current
instrument \(\Ipoly\), the saturated current and predictive observable
families \(\EQbang\) and \(\EMbang\), the quotients \(\Qsat\) and
\(\Msat\), the comparison map \(\ComparisonMap\), the autonomous lift
\(\OmegaSAT\), the visibility relation \(\VisBang\), the
currentization predicates \(\CurrentizeDec\) and \(\CurrentizeWit\),
the recognition source \(\CSLSATHidden\), the standard SAT verifier
package, the Class-B basis \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}\), and the
\(\BirdInt\) judgment package.

The AOR instance object
\[
  C_{\mathrm{PvNP}}(\Tsat,\Ipoly,\CSLSATHidden)
\]
has the following typed fields.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The carrier is \(\Hsat\), read through the finite-stage
        carriers described in \Cref{def:pvnp:history-carrier} and the
        saturated aggregate of \Cref{def:pvnp:saturated-closure}.
  \item The current observations are the lawful polynomial-time
        observables \(\EQbang\) of \Cref{def:pvnp:e-q-saturation}
        under the instrument \(\Ipoly\) of \Cref{def:pvnp:i-poly}.
        The predictive observations are \(\EMbang\).
  \item The current and predictive quotients are \(\Qsat\) and
        \(\Msat\), with comparison map \(\ComparisonMap\), as in
        \Cref{def:pvnp:q-saturated,def:pvnp:m-saturated,def:pvnp:comparison-map}.
  \item The routes are the polynomial-time post-processing, finite
        product, and composition operations of
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:e-q-closure-properties}, together with the
        self-reduction route used in Translation Theorem~B.
  \item The source records are the standard \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\)
        bridge used in Translation Theorem~A, the self-reduction
        package used in Translation Theorem~B, the standard verifier
        package for \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\), and the recognition source
        \(\CSLSATHidden\) supplied by \citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026}.
  \item The hidden-state record is the autonomous lift \(\OmegaSAT\)
        of \Cref{def:pvnp:omega-sat}, together with the visibility
        relation \(\VisBang\) of \Cref{def:pvnp:vis-bang}.
  \item The target records are decision currentization
        \(\CurrentizeDec(\mathrm{SAT})\), witness currentization
        \(\CurrentizeWit(\OmegaSAT)\), the localized fixed-branch
        residual
        \(\mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\notin\EQbang\),
        and the judgment proposition \(\PSB\neq\NPSB\).
  \item The residual statuses are the discharges recorded in
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:mechanical-records},
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:recognition-source-discharge},
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:translation-discharge},
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:class-b-scope-fence}, and
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:judgment-package}.
  \item The nonclaim register is the register of \Cref{sec:scope},
        including the absence of an unconditional standard-ZFC
        theorem, the absence of a claim to circumvent classical
        barriers in their native formulations, the non-derivation of
        \(\CSLSATHidden\), and the scoped nature of Class-B
        Irremovability.
\end{enumerate}
\footnote{Realized in Lean by the AOR-instance object declaration
listed in \Cref{app:formalization}; carrier-attached to the concrete
PvNP types.}

conclusion: The saturated SAT shell carries the following six mechanisms. P_ 1 , machine update. This is the deterministic polynomial-time transducer class admitted on the SAT layer, namely the class K_ poly declared in the audited shell. Update is by lawful polynomial-time machine action on encoded SAT instances. P_ 2 , admissibility. This is the set of encoded SAT instances admitted at the current finite stage. Admissibility is determined by the finite-stage restriction of the audited shell's instance database, together with the type-correctness and no-smuggling checks imposed by the lawfulness discipline. P_ 3 , timescale. This is the polynomial budget declared by the lawful instrument I_ poly , including the local clock and the time certificate recorded by each lawful current observable. P_ 4 , lens selection. This is the visibility lens of the audited shell, determining which projection of histories is exposed to current observation, and which wider projection is used for predictive observation. P_ 5 , packaging. This is the Q/M quotient and continuation packaging: the SAT-saturated current and predictive quotients Q^ ! _ SAT and M^ ! _ SAT , together with the comparison map pi^ ! on the history carrier H^ ! _ SAT . P_ 6 , audit. This is the audit ledger of the audited shell, including the machine-index record, time certificate, replay log, and gate predicates declared in the audit interface. The closed audit record is part of the saturated SAT layer T^ ! _ SAT , and the seven gates G_ 1 – G_ 7 are listed in .

\label{def:pvnp:six-mechanisms}
The saturated SAT shell carries the following six mechanisms.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(P_{1}\), \emph{machine update}.  This is the deterministic
  polynomial-time transducer class admitted on the SAT layer, namely
  the class \(K_{\mathrm{poly}}\) declared in the audited shell.
  Update is by lawful polynomial-time machine action on encoded SAT
  instances.

  \item \(P_{2}\), \emph{admissibility}.  This is the set of encoded
  SAT instances admitted at the current finite stage.  Admissibility is
  determined by the finite-stage restriction of the audited shell's
  instance database, together with the type-correctness and
  no-smuggling checks imposed by the lawfulness discipline.

  \item \(P_{3}\), \emph{timescale}.  This is the polynomial budget
  declared by the lawful instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\), including the local
  clock and the time certificate recorded by each lawful current
  observable.

  \item \(P_{4}\), \emph{lens selection}.  This is the visibility lens
  of the audited shell, determining which projection of histories is
  exposed to current observation, and which wider projection is used
  for predictive observation.

  \item \(P_{5}\), \emph{packaging}.  This is the \(Q/M\) quotient and
  continuation packaging: the SAT-saturated current and predictive
  quotients \(Q^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) and \(M^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), together with the comparison map
  \(\pi^{!}\) on the history carrier \(H^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\).

  \item \(P_{6}\), \emph{audit}.  This is the audit ledger of the
  audited shell, including the machine-index record, time certificate,
  replay log, and gate predicates declared in the audit interface.  The
  closed audit record is part of the saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), and
  the seven gates \(G_{1}\)--\(G_{7}\) are listed in
  \Cref{app:gate-audit}.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: [Class-B carrier-property law] A Class-B carrier-property law is a theorem of the form Phi( C) implies O∈ O_ C : T(O), where C is a Six Birds carrier, Phi( C) is an intrinsic feature of that carrier, and the impossibility conclusion follows from the feature itself. The feature is not an external recognition source, is not a restatement of the target, and is not a claim-discipline restriction on how the target is allowed to be asserted. Class-B laws are contrasted with Class-A claim-discipline laws. Class-A laws, such as no-overread, adequacy, and quotientality, act on the structure of the claim being made. Class-B laws act on the carrier: they try to derive an impossibility from a property of the computational substrate. The formalization records the intrinsic feature condition, the non-recognition-source condition, the non-claim-discipline condition, and the carrier-feature impossibility conclusion as explicit fields of the corresponding typed record.

\begin{definition}[Class-B carrier-property law]
\label{def:pvnp:class-b-law}
A \emph{Class-B carrier-property law} is a theorem of the form
\[
  \Phi(\mathcal C) \Longrightarrow
  \neg \exists O\in\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}\,:\,T(O),
\]
where \(\mathcal C\) is a Six Birds carrier, \(\Phi(\mathcal C)\) is
an intrinsic feature of that carrier, and the impossibility conclusion
follows from the feature itself.  The feature is not an external
recognition source, is not a restatement of the target, and is not a
claim-discipline restriction on how the target is allowed to be
asserted.
\end{definition}

Class-B laws are contrasted with Class-A claim-discipline laws.
Class-A laws, such as no-overread, adequacy, and quotientality, act on
the structure of the claim being made.  Class-B laws act on the
carrier: they try to derive an impossibility from a property of the
computational substrate.  The formalization records the intrinsic
feature condition, the non-recognition-source condition, the
non-claim-discipline condition, and the carrier-feature impossibility
conclusion as explicit fields of the corresponding typed record.

conclusion: For the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier, the fixed-presentation feature basis is B_ fix = \ Delta_X,\ PolyClosure(E^ ! _ Q ),\ TimeFilt,\ PresData\ . Here Delta_X is the diagonal equality relation on the encoded input carrier; PolyClosure(E^ ! _ Q ) is the closure structure of the saturated current-observable family under pairing, finite products, polynomial-time post-processing, and polynomial-time composition; TimeFilt is the polynomial resource ladder E^ [1] ⊆ E^ [2] ⊆ , E^ ! _ Q = _k E^ [k] ; and PresData is the fixed-presentation structural data: bit positions, variable names, symbol order, clause order, delimiter conventions, and the analogous features of the chosen SAT encoding.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:pvnp:basis-fix}
For the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier, the
\emph{fixed-presentation feature basis} is
\[
  \mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}
  =
  \{\Delta_X,\ \mathsf{PolyClosure}(E^{!}_{Q}),\
    \mathsf{TimeFilt},\ \mathsf{PresData}\}.
\]
Here \(\Delta_X\) is the diagonal equality relation on the encoded
input carrier; \(\mathsf{PolyClosure}(E^{!}_{Q})\) is the closure
structure of the saturated current-observable family under pairing,
finite products, polynomial-time post-processing, and polynomial-time
composition; \(\mathsf{TimeFilt}\) is the polynomial resource ladder
\[
  E^{[1]}\subseteq E^{[2]}\subseteq \cdots,
  \qquad
  E^{!}_{Q}=\bigcup_k E^{[k]};
\]
and \(\mathsf{PresData}\) is the fixed-presentation structural data:
bit positions, variable names, symbol order, clause order, delimiter
conventions, and the analogous features of the chosen SAT encoding.

source_wording_tex:
\label{def:pvnp:basis-fix}
For the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier, the
\emph{fixed-presentation feature basis} is
\[
  \mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}
  =
  \{\Delta_X,\ \mathsf{PolyClosure}(\EQbang),\
    \mathsf{TimeFilt},\ \mathsf{PresData}\}.
\]
Here \(\Delta_X\) is the diagonal equality relation on the encoded
input carrier; \(\mathsf{PolyClosure}(\EQbang)\) is the closure
structure of the saturated current-observable family under pairing,
finite products, polynomial-time post-processing, and polynomial-time
composition; \(\mathsf{TimeFilt}\) is the polynomial resource ladder
\[
  E^{[1]}\subseteq E^{[2]}\subseteq \cdots,
  \qquad
  \EQbang=\bigcup_k E^{[k]};
\]
and \(\mathsf{PresData}\) is the fixed-presentation structural data:
bit positions, variable names, symbol order, clause order, delimiter
conventions, and the analogous features of the chosen SAT encoding.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:pvnp:normal-classes}
The five \emph{normal feature classes} are \(Q,J,C,P,T\).
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(Q\), the \emph{quotient class}, consists of equivalence
  relations \(R\subseteq X\times X\) such that the proposed Class-B
  law requires \(R\subseteq\ker(F)\) for every \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\).
  Equivalently, every lawful current observable is required to be
  constant on \(R\)-classes.

  \item \(J\), the \emph{joint-access class}, consists of finite
  tuples \(F_1,\ldots,F_n\inE^{!}_{Q}\) of separately current
  observables whose joint access \((F_1,\ldots,F_n)\) is alleged not
  to lie in \(E^{!}_{Q}\).

  \item \(C\), the \emph{positive-closure class}, consists of
  constructions that yield new current observables from current ones
  by composition, pairing, products, or polynomial-time
  post-processing.

  \item \(P\), the \emph{presentation-refinement class}, consists of
  refinements of the carrier by presentation data.  These refinements
  supply breaker data rather than invariance constraints.

  \item \(T\), the \emph{time-filtration class}, consists of features
  indexed by polynomial resource strata \(E^{[k]}\), either at a fixed
  \(k\) or uniformly across all \(k\).
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: A basis-generated feature expression is built from B_ fix by finitely many applications of the following closure operations: quotienting, orbiting, transporting, holonomy or gluing-class formation, pairing, finite products, polynomial-time post-processing, resource filtration, and presentation refinement. This is the standard closure-operator construction on a basis of generators , restricted to the operations admitted by the carrier package. Transport has three flavors: route-equivalence transport, record-carrying transport, and resource-indexed transport. The normal-class assignment is a total function normalClass:\ basis-generated expressions\ \ Q,J,C,P,T\ . The diagonal primitive, quotienting, orbiting, transport-by-route, and holonomy or gluing-class formation land in Q . The polynomial-closure primitive, pairing, finite products, and polynomial-time post-processing land in C . The time-filtration primitive, transport-by-resource, and resource filtration land in T . The presentation primitive, transport-by-record, and presentation refinement land in P . Joint-access expressions land in J precisely when they assert obstruction to finite joint access of separately current observables.

\label{def:pvnp:basis-generated}
A \emph{basis-generated feature expression} is built from
\(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}\) by finitely many applications of the
following closure operations: quotienting, orbiting, transporting,
holonomy or gluing-class formation, pairing, finite products,
polynomial-time post-processing, resource filtration, and presentation
refinement.  This is the standard closure-operator construction on a
basis of generators \citep{DaveyPriestley2002LatticesOrder}, restricted
to the operations admitted by the carrier package.  Transport has three
flavors: route-equivalence transport, record-carrying transport, and
resource-indexed transport.

The normal-class assignment is a total function
\[
  \mathsf{normalClass}:\{\text{basis-generated expressions}\}
  \longrightarrow \{Q,J,C,P,T\}.
\]
The diagonal primitive, quotienting, orbiting,
transport-by-route, and holonomy or gluing-class formation land in
\(Q\).  The polynomial-closure primitive, pairing, finite products,
and polynomial-time post-processing land in \(C\).  The time-filtration
primitive, transport-by-resource, and resource filtration land in
\(T\).  The presentation primitive, transport-by-record, and
presentation refinement land in \(P\).  Joint-access expressions land
in \(J\) precisely when they assert obstruction to finite joint access
of separately current observables.

The functional-equation involution on the complex plane is

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:rh:nontrivial-zero-ledger}
Let
\[
  \Lambda_{\zeta}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)
\]
denote the completed Riemann zeta function
\citep{TitchmarshHeathBrown1986,Edwards1974}.  The nontrivial-zero
ledger of \(\Lambda_{\zeta}\) is the typed multiset
\[
  Z_{\zeta}^{\mathrm{nt}}
    =
  \bigl\{\,(\rho,m_{\rho}) :
      \rho\in\mathbb{C},
      \Lambda_{\zeta}(\rho)=0,
      0<\Real(\rho)<1,
      m_{\rho}>0
  \,\bigr\}_{\mathrm{multi}},
\]
where \(m_{\rho}\) is the positive integer multiplicity of \(\rho\)
as a zero of \(\Lambda_{\zeta}\).  The associated atomic ledger measure is
\(\mu_{L}(\{\rho\})=m_{\rho}\).

linear map
\[
  \DBG_{J,t}\colon E_{J,t}\to Z_J ,

velocity.  The right-support constraint
\(\DBG_{J,t}=\DBG_{J,t}\cdot P_{J(t)}\) records that
\(\DBG_{J,t}\) sees only the active shell at stage \(J\).

\label{def:ns:bg-package}
At each Bradshaw--Grujic stage \(j\), the \emph{BG-windowed
exact package} \(\Gamma_j\) collects the admissible
BG-window probes (the relevant components of
\(\Lphys_{J,t}\) and the windowed value of \(\DBG_{J,t}\)
on the active shell \(P_j\)) together with the structural
constraints they must preserve:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item the divergence-free condition \(\nabla\cdot u=0\);
  \item the Helmholtz-projected carrier
    \citep{Galdi2011} on which the probes act;
  \item the boundary arrangement relating \(P_j\) to
    \(P_{j+1}\);
  \item the doubling relation
    \(\lambda_{j+1}=2\lambda_j\).
\end{enumerate}
The package is \emph{exact} in the sense of
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}: it transports the audited
sub-problem from one BG window to the next without
altering the energy, response, or residual information.

\label{def:ns:null-mode-legal-ns}
The \emph{NS carrier} \((E_{J,t},C_{J,t},L^{\mathrm{phys}},D^{\mathrm{BG}})\) is
\emph{null-mode legal} when the physical-native probes and
the dissolving readout both vanish on the audit kernel:
\[
  \Lphys_{J,t}\big|_{\Ker C_{J,t}}=0,
  \qquad
  \DBG_{J,t}\big|_{\Ker C_{J,t}}=0 .
\]
Equivalently, both families descend to the legal energy
quotient \(E_{J,t}/\Ker C_{J,t}\), on which the audit form
is positive definite and the adequacy residual
\(\Xi_{C_{J,t}}(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\midL^{\mathrm{phys}})\) of
\citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion} is well-defined.  Null-mode
legality is built into the carrier by construction; it is
not a regularity assumption to be verified after the
residual has been formed.

\label{def:ns:bkm-import}
The \emph{Beale--Kato--Majda continuation criterion}
\citep{BealeKatoMajda1984,MajdaBertozzi2002,RobinsonRodrigoSadowski2016}
is the imported record asserting that for a strong solution
\(u\) of the Navier--Stokes equations on \([0,T)\) with
\(T\leT_{\max}(u_0)\) and \(\omega=\nabla\times u\),
\[
  \int_0^T \|\omega(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty}\,dt < \infty
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  T_{\max}(u_0)>T .
\]
The record is consumed at its declared status, with the
continuation conclusion supplied by the cited references
rather than derived here.

\label{def:ns:kato-import}
The \emph{Kato local well-posedness import}
\citep{Kato1972,FujitaKato1964,RobinsonRodrigoSadowski2016}
is the imported record asserting that for divergence-free
smooth Sobolev data on \(\mathbb R^3\) with
\(\gamma_0>5/2\),
\[
  \nabla\cdot u_0=0,\quad u_0\in H^{\gamma_0}(\mathbb R^3)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \exists\,T_{\max}(u_0)\in(0,\infty]\text{ and a unique }
  u\in C\bigl([0,T_{\max}(u_0)),H^{\gamma_0}\bigr).
\]
The carrier objects \(E_{J,t}\), \(C_{J,t}\),
\(\Lphys_{J,t}\), and \(\DBG_{J,t}\) of
\Cref{sec:ns-carrier} are all attached to this
strong-solution arc.

\label{def:ns:wang-halflog-import}
The \emph{half-log analyticity import}, in the
Foias--Temam tradition \citep{FoiasTemam1989} refined to
half-log form by \citet{HerbstSkibsted2011} and by the
preprint \citep{Wang2025AnalyticityRefined}, is the

\]
yields a lower bound on the spatial analyticity radius
\(\rho(t)\): on BG-compatible stages,
\[
  \rho(t)\gtrsim \frac{\log\lambda_J(t)}{\lambda_J(t)} .
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:ns:source-admission-ledger}
The \emph{source-admission ledger} is the positive
operator-valued sum
\[
  \Omega_{\mathrm{src}} = \Omega_{\mathrm{tr}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{pr}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{visc}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{tail}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{str}} ,
\]
with five positive semidefinite components
\[
  \Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\succeq 0,
\]
hence \(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}\succeq 0\).  The summands record the
contributions entering the dissolving response space at each
stage from, respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item the nonlinear transport \((u\cdot\nabla)u\) as a Schur
    block on the active shells (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}\));
  \item the pressure \(\nabla p\) after the Helmholtz/Leray
    projection (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}\));
  \item viscosity \(\nu\Delta u\) as a damping block on each
    shell (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}\));
  \item the high-frequency tail capturing the interaction of
    visible shells with discarded shells \(j>J\)
    (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}\));
  \item vortex stretching \((\omega\cdot\nabla)u\) tested
    against the physical-native probes (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\)).
\end{enumerate}
Each summand is owned by an imported PDE record from
\Cref{sec:imports}: \(\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}\) by the
Littlewood--Paley / Bony--Chemin--Danchin commutator and
Helmholtz-projection estimates
(\Cref{def:ns:lp-bcd-import}); \(\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}\) by the viscous
damping at scale \(\lambda_J(t)\) from \(\nu\Delta\);
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}\) by the Sobolev/Besov embedding combined with
the BG-window cutoff (\Cref{def:ns:sobolev-besov-embedding-import});
and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\) by the vortex-stretching estimate against
the physical-native probes.

with five positive semidefinite components
\[
  \Omtr\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Ompr\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omvisc\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omtail\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omstr\succeq 0,
\]
hence \(\Omsrc\succeq 0\).  The summands record the
contributions entering the dissolving response space at each
stage from, respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item the nonlinear transport \((u\cdot\nabla)u\) as a Schur
    block on the active shells (\(\Omtr\));
  \item the pressure \(\nabla p\) after the Helmholtz/Leray
    projection (\(\Ompr\));
  \item viscosity \(\nu\Delta u\) as a damping block on each
    shell (\(\Omvisc\));
  \item the high-frequency tail capturing the interaction of
    visible shells with discarded shells \(j>J\)
    (\(\Omtail\));
  \item vortex stretching \((\omega\cdot\nabla)u\) tested
    against the physical-native probes (\(\Omstr\)).
\end{enumerate}
Each summand is owned by an imported PDE record from
\Cref{sec:imports}: \(\Omtr\) and \(\Ompr\) by the
Littlewood--Paley / Bony--Chemin--Danchin commutator and
Helmholtz-projection estimates
(\Cref{def:ns:lp-bcd-import}); \(\Omvisc\) by the viscous
damping at scale \(\lambdaJ(t)\) from \(\nu\Delta\);
\(\Omtail\) by the Sobolev/Besov embedding combined with
the BG-window cutoff (\Cref{def:ns:sobolev-besov-embedding-import});
and \(\Omstr\) by the vortex-stretching estimate against
the physical-native probes.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:work-cap-div}
Let $w,\mathrm{Cap}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ be sequences with $\mathrm{Cap}(n)>0$.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{WORK:} $w(n)$ is the ``work quantum'' required to advance from level $n$ to $n+1$.
\item \textbf{CAP:} $\mathrm{Cap}(n)$ is the ``capacity'' available at level $n$ (a bound relating work
to input energy and/or throughput on the crossing interval).
\item \textbf{WORK$\times$CAP inequality:} for all $n$,
\[
w(n)\ \le\ \mathrm{Cap}(n)\,\bigl(t(n+1)-t(n)\bigr).
\]
\item \textbf{DIV:} the ratios $w(n)/\mathrm{Cap}(n)$ have unbounded partial sums:
\[
\forall M\in\mathbb{R},\ \exists n\in\mathbb{N}\ \text{s.t.}\ M \le \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{w(k)}{\mathrm{Cap}(k)}.
\]
\end{itemize}

WORK × CAP inequality: for all n , w(n)\ \ Cap(n) (t(n+1)-t(n) ). DIV: the ratios w(n)/Cap(n) have unbounded partial sums: M∈R,\ n∈N\ s.t.\ M _ k=0 ^ n-1 w(k) Cap(k) .
source_wording_tex:
\label{def:work-cap-div}
Let $w,\mathrm{Cap}:\N\to\R$ be sequences with $\mathrm{Cap}(n)>0$.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{WORK:} $w(n)$ is the ``work quantum'' required to advance from level $n$ to $n+1$.
\item \textbf{CAP:} $\mathrm{Cap}(n)$ is the ``capacity'' available at level $n$ (a bound relating work
to input energy and/or throughput on the crossing interval).
\item \textbf{WORK$\times$CAP inequality:} for all $n$,
\[
w(n)\ \le\ \mathrm{Cap}(n)\,\bigl(t(n+1)-t(n)\bigr).
\]
\item \textbf{DIV:} the ratios $w(n)/\mathrm{Cap}(n)$ have unbounded partial sums:
\[
\forall M\in\R,\ \exists n\in\N\ \text{s.t.}\ M \le \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{w(k)}{\mathrm{Cap}(k)}.
\]
\end{itemize}

conclusion: Throughout, ``SBT-legal'' is used in two explicit senses. Analytically, it denotes a restricted variant/theory in which feasibility at each scale excludes wavepacket-like concentration (a hypothesis on admissible interface signals, not a theorem about classical Navier–Stokes). Operationally, we implement a certificate that tests this exclusion at a chosen resolution and time window; in this paper we use it primarily as an initial-data filter and as a controlled LEGAL-vs-ILLEGAL diagnostic. We do not claim that passing the certificate at t=0 implies it remains true for later times under the classical PDE flow; that invariance problem is recorded as an OPEN hinge in Section . This section states the paper's main proposal: rather than claiming Clay regularity, we define an SBT-legal (restricted) variant of Navier–Stokes in which feasibility (P2) excludes localization in a quantitative way, and we provide a reproducible certificate to test this legality on initial data (and diagnostically along short runs). This is a research program specification and an operational toolbox, not a PDE theorem.

\label{def:spt-legal-cert}
Given a dyadic decomposition $u_0=\sum_j (u_0)_j$, define $L_j(u_0)$ by \eqref{eq:local-energy-fraction}.
Let $f_j$ denote the baseline volume fraction at scale $j$ (uniform reference).
Define the normalized concentration factor
\[
\kappa_j(u_0) \;:=\; \frac{L_j(u_0)}{f_j}.
\]
We say $u_0$ is \emph{SBT-legal at thresholds} $(\kappa_\star,\mathrm{burst}_\star,m_\star)$
if the certificate computed by the script
\nolinkurl{python/scripts/ns_spt_legal_certify.py}
returns PASS, which in practice checks configurable bounds on:
(i) $\max_j \kappa_j$,
(ii) a burst ratio statistic over time windows if evolution is enabled,
and optionally (iii) an effective channel count $m_{95}$ from PCA/SVD diagnostics.

conclusion: Fix a microstate space Z , a lens f : Z → X , and an evaluation window tau . A logic layer at (f,tau) consists of a nontrivial family B ⊆ Sigma_f of binary packaged predicates together with induced macro-updates such that: Stability. Each b ∈ B is metastable on the timescale tau . Closure. The relevant micro-updates descend to macro-operators on the packaged variables with small closure defect. Feasibility semantics. Each b ∈ B is the indicator of a stable feasible set, and the connective operations required at the layer remain definable there. Auditability. Persistence, route agreement, and information loss are measurable by explicit diagnostics. When these conditions fail, a symbolic description may still be convenient, but it does not constitute a closed logic layer in the sense used in this paper.

conclusion: Definition is intentionally stricter than merely being able to label states by zero and one. A candidate bit must remain stable long enough to matter, must support a descended operator calculus, and must survive audit. This is why the six primitives are complementary rather than redundant. P5 packages the carrier; P4 keeps it from dissolving immediately; P2 makes it semantically meaningful; P1 determines whether an effective operator vocabulary can be stabilized; P3 detects route dependence and protocol residue; P6 determines what must be paid to maintain the whole arrangement.

conclusion: Definition gives four requirements for a logic layer: stability, closure, feasibility semantics, and auditability. This section turns those four requirements into measurable quantities and summarizes the controlled laboratories in which they are evaluated. The important methodological point is that the paper is not reporting live computations from the manuscript source. All numerical values reported in Sections – are taken from the frozen result bundle under results/final_claims/ and the source artifacts it summarizes. The manuscript does not recompute those values during drafting; it only defines the diagnostics and interprets the frozen outputs. Methodologically, this follows the broader Six Birds insistence that closure claims be paired with explicit audit rather than inferred from symbolic convenience alone .

Let parameters be partitioned as $\theta=(\phi,\eta_B)$ where $\phi$ denotes the shared parameters we hold fixed in the audit direction $B|A$ and $\eta_B$ denotes nuisance parameters specific to lens $B$. Define the profiled log-likelihood
\begin{equation}
  \log \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_B(\phi) \;\equiv\; \max_{\eta_B}\, \log \mathcal{L}_B(\phi,\eta_B),
  \label{eq:profile_loglike}
\end{equation}
and the profiled directional mismatch
\begin{equation}
  \widetilde{\Delta \chi^2}_{B|A} \;\equiv\; -2\left[\log \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_B(\hat\phi_A) - \log \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_B(\hat\phi_B)\right],
  \label{eq:profile_dchi}
\end{equation}
where $\hat\phi_L$ is the shared-parameter component of the best-fit point under lens $L$.
In practice we approximate \cref{eq:profile_loglike} by profiling only a tractable subset of $B$'s nuisance parameters under a runtime cap; the intent is not to ``profile away'' all mismatch, but to reduce sensitivity to purely lens-specific packaging degrees of freedom.
